verses.science: न्यवसं पूजितस्तत्र भोजवृष्ण्यन्धकोत्तमै: ततः कदाचिद् धर्मात्मा दीक्षितो मधुसूदनः। जो बार-बार किया जाता है, वह अगली प्रवृत्ति को मजबूत करता है। यह पंक्ति कर्म को उसी चक्र के रूप में देखती है।

verses.sanskrit: स सन्नोदयितव्यस्ते तावुद्दिश्य वनौकसौ । वसुदेवसुतौ वीरौ यथा स्यातां गतायुषौ ३२॥ त्वया चैव गजेन्द्रेण यदि तौ गोष्ठजीविनौ । भवेतां पतितौ रङ्गे पश्येयमहमुत्कटौ ॥ ३३ ॥
verses.transliteration: sa sannodayitavyaste tāvuddiśya vanaukasau | vasudevasutau vīrau yathā syātāṃ gatāyuṣau 32|| tvayā caiva gajendreṇa yadi tau goṣṭhajīvinau | bhavetāṃ patitau raṅge paśyeyamahamutkaṭau || 33 ||

verses.sanskrit: ततस्तौ पतितौ दृष्ट्वा वसुदेवः सबान्धवः । छिन्नमूलो निरालम्बः सभार्यो विनशिष्यति ॥ ३४ ॥
verses.transliteration: tatastau patitau dṛṣṭvā vasudevaḥ sabāndhavaḥ | chinnamūlo nirālambaḥ sabhāryo vinaśiṣyati || 34 ||
verses.translation: Vaishampāyana said:—The sage Narada then repaired to the residence of Mahendra; and there he passed the night in witnessing the festivities (held in honor of Siva) (1). The illustrious Adityas, the best of gods, the Vasus, the learned Rajarshis who had attained to paradise through their meritorious deeds (2), the Nagas, the Yakshas, the Siddhas, the Charanas, the sages of ascetic austerities, Brahmharsis by thousands, Devarshis and Moonies (3), the high-souled Saparnas, the highly powerful Marutas, and hundreds of other divine creatures were assembled there (4). The god Maheswara of immeasurable energy, accompanied by Uma and surrounded by his attendants sat at the head of them all (5). That protector of all creatures was surrounded also by those foremost of the Devarshis who suffer no decay even at the end of thousands of Kalpas, (6) who are worshipped by gods equal to Indra, are possessed of self-knowledge, free from pride and who ever tread the path of rectitude (7). The Rudras the progeny of Kasyapa, Skanda, the god of fire, that best of rivers Ganga, Archisman, Tamburu, Bharisa, that foremost of eloquent speakers, those possessed of the ascetic merit, and such other leaders of the divine host, then O Bharata, adored that supreme god Siva (8–9). O ruler of men, other gods devoted to religious ways and austerities and followers of the path of the pious,—followed their above-named leaders (i.e., offered homages to Siva), (10). O king, those men who desirous of good, worship the gods on earth, those men are in their turned worshipped in heaven by the immortals desirous of securing good (11). O descendant of the Kouravas, those men versed in the Vedas, who live according to the ordinances of the Sastras and who adore the gods in the performance of their religious ceremonies for the benefit of their ancestral manes, those are held in high estimation in the next world by the gods (12). O ruler of men, there the illustrious Chitraratha, the king of the Gandharvas together with his son, delightfully played upon the heavenly musical instruments (13). Urnayu, Chitrasena, Hahahuhu, Dumbara, Tamvura and other Gandharvas sang the six different harmonies (14). Urvasi, Viprachiti, Hemā, Rambhā, Hemadantā Ghritachi, and Sahajanyā and other damsels then performed numerous kinds of dances there (15). The self-possessed illustrious Siva accepted these homages with pleasure, and that lord of the world pleased with these worshipful acts of Sakra, went back to his own residence (16).
verses.hindi: भगवान् श्रीकृष्ण बोले--द्विजश्रेष्ठ ! तुम्हें डरना नहीं चाहिए। में तुम्हारी रक्षा करूँगा। तुम्हारा भला हो, ठीक-ठीक बताओ तुम्हें किससे भय है? यदि अत्यन्त दुष्कर कार्य हो तो भी उसे कहनेमें संकोच त्रयो हताश्चतुर्थ त्वं कृष्ण रक्षितुमहसि। ब्राह्मण्या: सूतिकालोउद्य तत्र रक्षा विधीयताम्। यथा श्रियेदपत्यं मे तथा कुरु जनार्दन रक्षा च ब्राह्मणे कार्या सर्वावस्थागतैरपि
verses.wordMeaning: Vaishampāyana said:—The sage Narada then repaired to the residence of Mahendra; and there he passed the night in witnessing the festivities (held in honor of Siva) (1). The illustrious Adityas, the best of gods, the Vasus,…
verses.commentary: Sense: Vaishampāyana said:—The sage Narada then repaired to the residence of Mahendra; and there he passed the night in witnessing the festivities (held in honor of Siva) (1). The illustrious Adityas, the best of gods, the Vasus,…
verses.science: भगवान् श्रीकृष्ण बोले--द्विजश्रेष्ठ ! तुम्हें डरना नहीं चाहिए। इसे किसी एक घटना का संयोग न मानकर एक नियम की तरह पढ़ना इस पंक्ति का बल है।

verses.sanskrit: ये चेमे यादवा मूर्खाः सर्वे कृष्णपरायणाः । विनशिष्यन्ति च्छिन्नाशा दृष्ट्वा कृष्णं निपातितम् ॥ ३५ ॥
verses.transliteration: ye ceme yādavā mūrkhāḥ sarve kṛṣṇaparāyaṇāḥ | vinaśiṣyanti cchinnāśā dṛṣṭvā kṛṣṇaṃ nipātitam || 35 ||
verses.translation: On the departure of that lord of the created beings, the kings (assembled there) returned to the places whence they came; the gods also honored by Mahendra repaired to their respective abodes (17). When everybody had gone away and Purandara was seated comfortably with his own courtiers, the sage Narada approached him (18). Rising from his seat, Indra received that sage of ascetic wealth, and offered him a seat made of Kusa grass equal to that of his own (19). Thereafter the highly powerful Narada said these words to Mahendra:—"O foremost of immortals, know me now to be the messenger from Vishnu of matchless might (20). I have been despatched here by that illustrious one of immense powers on a mission that will remove one of his causes of pain" (21). Thereupon greeting the sage with sweet and agreeable words, the illustrious Pākasasana said with delight (22):—"O sage, tell me without delay what has that foremost of men said; it is after a long time that the high-souled Krishna has remembered us (23)".
verses.hindi: श्रुत्वाहमेवं कृष्णस्थ वचो5वोचं नराधिप। मां नियोजय गोविन्द रक्षिष्ये5हं द्विज॑ं भयात्  एकादशाधिकशततमो5ध्याय:  ब्राह्मणने कहा--महाबाहो! निष्पाप श्रीकृष्ण! जब-जब मेरे पुत्र पैदा होता है, तब-तब काल उसे हर ले जाता है। इस प्रकार मेरे तीन पुत्र हर लिये गये। अब चौथा पुत्र होनेवाला है, अत: आप ही उसकी रक्षा करनेयोग्य हैं॥ ११ ॥ जनार्दन! आज ब्राह्मणी (मेरी पत्नी)-के प्रसवका समय है, अतः वहाँ रक्षा कीजिये। यह मेरी संतान जिस तरह भी जीवित बच जाय, वह उपाय कीजिये अर्जुन कहते हैं--तब भगवान् गोविन्दने मुझसे कहा--पार्थ! मैं तो यज्ञकी दीक्षा ले चुका, परंतु सभी अवस्थाओंमें भी ब्राह्मणकी रक्षा तो करनी ही चाहिए'
verses.wordMeaning: On the departure of that lord of the created beings, the kings (assembled there) returned to the places whence they came; the gods also honored by Mahendra repaired to their respective abodes (17).…
verses.commentary: Sense: On the departure of that lord of the created beings, the kings (assembled there) returned to the places whence they came; the gods also honored by Mahendra repaired to their respective abodes (17).…
verses.science: श्रुत्वाहमेवं कृष्णस्थ वचो5वोचं नराधिप। जो बार-बार किया जाता है, वह अगली प्रवृत्ति को मजबूत करता है। यह पंक्ति कर्म को उसी चक्र के रूप में देखती है।

verses.sanskrit: एतौ हत्वा गजेन्द्रेण मल्लैर्वा स्वयमेव वा । पुरीं निर्यादवीं कृत्वा विचरिष्याम्यहं सुखी ॥ ३६ ॥
verses.transliteration: etau hatvā gajendreṇa mallairvā svayameva vā | purīṃ niryādavīṃ kṛtvā vicariṣyāmyahaṃ sukhī || 36 ||

verses.sanskrit: करके मैं सुखपूर्वक विचरूँगा ॥ ३६ ॥
verses.transliteration: karake maiṃ sukhapūrvaka vicarū~gā || 36 ||

verses.sanskrit: पिता हि मे परित्यक्तो यादवानां कुलोद्वहः । शेषाश्च मे परित्यक्ता यादवाः कृष्णपक्षिणः ॥ ३७ ॥
verses.transliteration: pitā hi me parityakto yādavānāṃ kulodvahaḥ | śeṣāśca me parityaktā yādavāḥ kṛṣṇapakṣiṇaḥ || 37 ||

verses.sanskrit: न चाहमुग्रसेनेन जातः किल सुतार्थिना । मानुषेणाल्पवीर्येण यथा मामाह नारदः ॥ ३८ ॥
verses.transliteration: na cāhamugrasenena jātaḥ kila sutārthinā | mānuṣeṇālpavīryeṇa yathā māmāha nāradaḥ || 38 ||

verses.sanskrit: कथमुक्तं नारदेन राजन् देवर्षिणा पुरा । आश्चर्यमेतत् कथितं त्वत्तः श्रुतमरिन्दम ॥ ३९ ॥
verses.transliteration: kathamuktaṃ nāradena rājan devarṣiṇā purā | āścaryametat kathitaṃ tvattaḥ śrutamarindama || 39 ||

verses.sanskrit: कथमन्येन जातस्त्वमुग्रसेनात् पितुर्विना । तव मात्रा कथं राजन् कृतं कर्मेदमीदृशम् ॥ ४० ॥
verses.transliteration: kathamanyena jātastvamugrasenāt piturvinā | tava mātrā kathaṃ rājan kṛtaṃ karmedamīdṛśam || 40 ||

verses.sanskrit: अन्यापि प्राकृता नारी न कुर्याच्च जुगुप्सितम् । विस्तरं श्रोतुमिच्छामि ह्येतत् कौतूहलं हि मे ॥ ४१ ॥
verses.transliteration: anyāpi prākṛtā nārī na kuryācca jugupsitam | vistaraṃ śrotumicchāmi hyetat kautūhalaṃ hi me || 41 ||

verses.sanskrit: यथा कथितवान् विप्रो महर्षिर्नारदः प्रभुः । तथाहं सम्प्रवक्ष्यामि यदि तै श्रवणे मतिः ॥ ४२ ॥
verses.transliteration: yathā kathitavān vipro maharṣirnāradaḥ prabhuḥ | tathāhaṃ sampravakṣyāmi yadi tai śravaṇe matiḥ || 42 ||

verses.sanskrit: आगतः शक्रसदनात् स वै शक्रसखो मुनिः । चन्द्रांशुशुक्लवसनो जटामण्डलमुद्वहन् ॥ ४३ ॥
verses.transliteration: āgataḥ śakrasadanāt sa vai śakrasakho muniḥ | candrāṃśuśuklavasano jaṭāmaṇḍalamudvahan || 43 ||

verses.sanskrit: कृष्णाजिनोत्तरीयेण रुक्मयज्ञोपवीतवान् । दण्डी कमण्डलुधरः प्रजापतिरिवापरः ॥ ४४ ॥
verses.transliteration: kṛṣṇājinottarīyeṇa rukmayajñopavītavān | daṇḍī kamaṇḍaludharaḥ prajāpatirivāparaḥ || 44 ||

verses.sanskrit: गाता चतुर्णां वेदानां विद्वान् गान्धर्ववेदवित् । स नारदोऽथ देवर्षिर्ब्रह्मलोकचरोऽव्ययः ॥ ४५ ॥
verses.transliteration: gātā caturṇāṃ vedānāṃ vidvān gāndharvavedavit | sa nārado'tha devarṣirbrahmalokacaro'vyayaḥ || 45 ||

verses.sanskrit: तमागतमृषिं दृष्ट्वा पूजयित्वा यथाविधि । पाद्यार्घ्यमासनं दत्त्वा सम्प्रवेश्योपविश्य ह ॥ ४६ ॥
verses.transliteration: tamāgatamṛṣiṃ dṛṣṭvā pūjayitvā yathāvidhi | pādyārghyamāsanaṃ dattvā sampraveśyopaviśya ha || 46 ||

verses.sanskrit: सुखोपविष्टोऽथ मुनिः पृष्ट्वा च कुशलं मम । उवाच च प्रीतमना देवर्षिर्भावितात्मवान् ॥ ४७ ॥
verses.transliteration: sukhopaviṣṭo'tha muniḥ pṛṣṭvā ca kuśalaṃ mama | uvāca ca prītamanā devarṣirbhāvitātmavān || 47 ||

verses.sanskrit: पूजितोऽहं त्वया वीर विधिदृष्टेन कर्मणा । इदमेकं मम वचः श्रूयतां प्रतिगृह्यताम् ॥ ४८ ॥
verses.transliteration: pūjito'haṃ tvayā vīra vidhidṛṣṭena karmaṇā | idamekaṃ mama vacaḥ śrūyatāṃ pratigṛhyatām || 48 ||

verses.sanskrit: गतोऽहं देवसदनं सौवर्णं मेरुपर्वतम् । सोऽहं कदाचिद् देवानां समाजे मेरुमूर्धनि ॥ ४९ ॥
verses.transliteration: gato'haṃ devasadanaṃ sauvarṇaṃ meruparvatam | so'haṃ kadācid devānāṃ samāje merumūrdhani || 49 ||

verses.sanskrit: तत्र मन्त्रयतामेवं देवतानां मया श्रुतः । भवतः सानुगम्यैव वधोपायः सुदारुणः ॥ ५० ॥
verses.transliteration: tatra mantrayatāmevaṃ devatānāṃ mayā śrutaḥ | bhavataḥ sānugamyaiva vadhopāyaḥ sudāruṇaḥ || 50 ||

verses.sanskrit: तत्र यो देवकीगर्भो विष्णुर्लोकनमस्कृतः । योऽस्या गर्भोऽष्टमः कंस स ते मृत्युर्भविष्यति ॥ ५१ ॥
verses.transliteration: tatra yo devakīgarbho viṣṇurlokanamaskṛtaḥ | yo'syā garbho'ṣṭamaḥ kaṃsa sa te mṛtyurbhaviṣyati || 51 ||

verses.sanskrit: देवानां स तु सर्वस्वं त्रिदिवस्य गतिश्च सः । परं रहस्यं देवानां स ते मृत्युर्भविष्यति ॥ ५२ ॥
verses.transliteration: devānāṃ sa tu sarvasvaṃ tridivasya gatiśca saḥ | paraṃ rahasyaṃ devānāṃ sa te mṛtyurbhaviṣyati || 52 ||

verses.sanskrit: यत्नश्च क्रियतां कंस गर्भाणां पातनं प्रति । नावज्ञा रिपवे कार्या दुर्बले स्वजनेऽपि वा ॥ ५३ ॥
verses.transliteration: yatnaśca kriyatāṃ kaṃsa garbhāṇāṃ pātanaṃ prati | nāvajñā ripave kāryā durbale svajane'pi vā || 53 ||

verses.sanskrit: न चायमुग्रसेनः स पिता तव महाबलः । द्रुमिलो नाम तेजस्वी सौभस्य पतिरूर्जितः ॥ ५४ ॥
verses.transliteration: na cāyamugrasenaḥ sa pitā tava mahābalaḥ | drumilo nāma tejasvī saubhasya patirūrjitaḥ || 54 ||

verses.sanskrit: श्रुत्वाहं तद् वचस्तस्य किञ्चिद् रोषसमन्वितः । भूयोऽपृच्छं कथं ब्रह्मन् द्रुमिलो नाम दानवः ॥ ५५ ॥
verses.transliteration: śrutvāhaṃ tad vacastasya kiñcid roṣasamanvitaḥ | bhūyo'pṛcchaṃ kathaṃ brahman drumilo nāma dānavaḥ || 55 ||

verses.sanskrit: मम मात्रा कथं तस्य ब्रूहि विप्र समागमः । एतदिच्छाम्यहं श्रोतुं विस्तरेण तपोधन ॥ ५६ ॥
verses.transliteration: mama mātrā kathaṃ tasya brūhi vipra samāgamaḥ | etadicchāmyahaṃ śrotuṃ vistareṇa tapodhana || 56 ||

verses.sanskrit: हन्त ते कथयिष्यामि शृणु राजन् यथार्थतः । द्रमिलस्य च मात्रा ते संवादं च समागमम् ॥ ५७ ॥
verses.transliteration: hanta te kathayiṣyāmi śṛṇu rājan yathārthataḥ | dramilasya ca mātrā te saṃvādaṃ ca samāgamam || 57 ||

verses.sanskrit: सुयामुनं नाम नगं तव माता रजस्वला । प्रेक्षितुं सहिता स्त्रीभिर्गता वै सा कुतूहलात् ॥ ५८ ॥
verses.transliteration: suyāmunaṃ nāma nagaṃ tava mātā rajasvalā | prekṣituṃ sahitā strībhirgatā vai sā kutūhalāt || 58 ||

verses.sanskrit: सा तत्र रमणीयेषु रुचिरद्रुमसानुषु । चचार नगशृङ्गेषु कन्दरेषु नदीषु च ॥ ५९ ॥
verses.transliteration: sā tatra ramaṇīyeṣu ruciradrumasānuṣu | cacāra nagaśṛṅgeṣu kandareṣu nadīṣu ca || 59 ||
verses.hindi: पहुँचा है, अब आपलोग इस तरह रहें, जिससे फिर धोखा न हो'॥ ८॥ फिर तो दो घड़ीमें ब्राह्मणके घरके भीतर दीनतापूर्वक रोदनकी ध्वनि मुझे सुनायी दी। लोग कह रहे थे--'हाय! बालकको हर ले जाता है, हर ले गया'॥९॥ फिर आकाशमें मैंने अपहत बालकका 'ऊँह' यह शब्द सुना; परंतु उसका अपहरण करनेवाले राक्षसको मैं नहीं देख पाता था॥१०॥ तात! तब हमलोगोंने बाण-वर्षा करके चारों ओरसे सम्पूर्ण दिशाओंको रूँंध डाला तो भी उस बालकका अपहरण तो हो ही गया॥११॥ उस कुमारका अपहरण हो जानेपर ब्राह्मणने आर्तनाद करके उस समय मुझे अत्यन्त कड़वी खरी-खोटी बातें सुनानी आरम्भ कीं वृथा त्वं स्पर्धसे नित्यं कृष्णेनामितबुद्धिना। यदि स्यादिह गोविन्दो नैतदत्याहितं भवेत्
verses.translation: ²⁸⁸ Literally his prowess and energy.
verses.explanation: पहुँचा है, अब आपलोग इस तरह रहें, जिससे फिर धोखा न हो'॥ ८॥ फिर तो दो घड़ीमें ब्राह्मणके घरके भीतर दीनतापूर्वक रोदनकी ध्वनि मुझे सुनायी दी। इस पंक्ति का बल इसी प्रसंग के नियम पर है, किसी अलग प्रसंग से लाई हुई सामान्य उक्ति पर नहीं।
verses.science: पहुँचा है, अब आपलोग इस तरह रहें, जिससे फिर धोखा न हो'॥ ८॥ फिर तो दो घड़ीमें ब्राह्मणके घरके भीतर दीनतापूर्वक रोदनकी ध्वनि मुझे सुनायी दी। जो विषय बार-बार मन में आता है, वही अगली क्रिया की दिशा बनता है। यह पंक्ति उसी मानसिक चयन को अपना विषय बनाती है।

verses.sanskrit: किन्नरोद्गीतमधुराः प्रतिश्रुत्यभिनादिताः । शृण्वन्ती काजननीर्वाचः श्रोत्रसुखावहाः ॥ ६० ॥
verses.transliteration: kinnarodgītamadhurāḥ pratiśrutyabhināditāḥ | śṛṇvantī kājananīrvācaḥ śrotrasukhāvahāḥ || 60 ||

verses.sanskrit: बर्हिणां चैव विरुतं खगानां च विकूजितम् । अभीक्ष्णमभिशृण्वन्ती स्त्रीधर्ममभिरोचयत् ॥ ६१ ॥
verses.transliteration: barhiṇāṃ caiva virutaṃ khagānāṃ ca vikūjitam | abhīkṣṇamabhiśṛṇvantī strīdharmamabhirocayat || 61 ||

verses.sanskrit: एतस्मिन्नन्तरे वायुर्वनराजिविनिःसृतः । हृद्यः कुसुमगन्धाढ्यो ववौ मन्मथबोधनः ॥ ६२ ॥
verses.transliteration: etasminnantare vāyurvanarājiviniḥsṛtaḥ | hṛdyaḥ kusumagandhāḍhyo vavau manmathabodhanaḥ || 62 ||
verses.hindi: चतुर्थाश फल पाता है, उसी प्रकार रक्षा न करनेवाला पुरुष अरक्षितके पापका भी भागी होता है॥ १६॥ तूने घोषणा तो की थी कि मैं रक्षा करूँगा, परंतु तू रक्षा करनेमें समर्थ नहीं है। तेरा यह गाण्डीव धनुष व्यर्थ है! तेरा पराक्रम और यश भी व्यर्थ ही है' उस ब्राह्मणसे कुछ न कहकर मैं वृष्णि और अन्धकवंशके उन राजकुमारोंके साथ प्रस्थित हो उस स्थानपर आया, जहाँ महातेजस्वी श्रीकृष्ण विराजमान थे॥ १८ ॥ द्वारकामें पहुँचकर मधुसूदनका दर्शन करके मैं लज्जित एवं शोकसे संतप्त हो उठा। गोविन्दने मेरी इस अवस्थाको लक्ष्य किया॥ १९॥ इसी बीचमें उस ब्राह्मणने आकर मुझे लज्जित देख भगवान् श्रीकृष्णफेक समीप ही इस तरह मूर्खता तो देखो। मैंने इस कायर या नपुंसककी बातपर विश्वास कर लिया॥२०॥ जहाँ प्रद्युम्म, अनिरुद्ध, बलराम और श्रीकृष्ण भी रक्षा करनेमें असमर्थ हों, वहाँ दूसरा कौन रक्षा कर सकता है ?॥ २१॥ व्यर्थ
verses.translation: ²⁸⁸ Literally his prowess and energy.
verses.explanation: चतुर्थाश फल पाता है, उसी प्रकार रक्षा न करनेवाला पुरुष अरक्षितके पापका भी भागी होता है॥ १६॥ तूने घोषणा तो की थी कि मैं रक्षा करूँगा, परंतु तू रक्षा करनेमें स…। इस पंक्ति का बल इसी प्रसंग के नियम पर है, किसी अलग प्रसंग से लाई हुई सामान्य उक्ति पर नहीं।
verses.science: चतुर्थाश फल पाता है, उसी प्रकार रक्षा न करनेवाला पुरुष अरक्षितके पापका भी भागी होता है॥ १६॥ तूने घोषणा तो की थी कि मैं रक्षा करूँगा, परंतु तू रक्षा करनेमें स…। धीमी श्वास वेगस तंत्रिका को सक्रिय कर भय-प्रतिक्रिया को शांत करती है। यह पंक्ति उसी श्वास और मन के संबंध को कहती है।

verses.sanskrit: द्विरेफाभरणाश्चैव कदम्बा वायुघट्टिताः । मुमुचुर्गन्धमधिकं सन्ततासारमूर्छिताः ॥ ६३ ॥
verses.transliteration: dvirephābharaṇāścaiva kadambā vāyughaṭṭitāḥ | mumucurgandhamadhikaṃ santatāsāramūrchitāḥ || 63 ||

verses.sanskrit: केसराः पुष्पवर्षैश्च ववृषुर्मदबोधनाः । नीपा दीपा इवाभान्ति पुष्पकण्टकधारिणः ॥ ६४ ॥
verses.transliteration: kesarāḥ puṣpavarṣaiśca vavṛṣurmadabodhanāḥ | nīpā dīpā ivābhānti puṣpakaṇṭakadhāriṇaḥ || 64 ||
verses.hindi: अतः उन्होंने जलती आगमें प्रवेश करनेका विचार दर्शये द्विजसूनुं ते मावज्ञात्मानमात्मना॥ २६ किया। उस समय श्रीकृष्ण और प्रद्यम्नने आकर उन्हें कीर्ति त एते विपुलां स्थापयिष्यन्ति मानवा:। इति सम्भाष्य मां स्नेहात् समाश्रास्य च माधव: आरोष् ब्राह्मणं कृष्णो हावरोप्य च दारुकम् ततः समास्थाय रथं कृष्णो5हं ब्राह्मण: स च।
verses.translation: ²⁸⁸ Literally his prowess and energy.
verses.explanation: अतः उन्होंने जलती आगमें प्रवेश करनेका विचार दर्शये द्विजसूनुं ते मावज्ञात्मानमात्मना॥ २६ किया। इस पंक्ति का बल इसी प्रसंग के नियम पर है, किसी अलग प्रसंग से लाई हुई सामान्य उक्ति पर नहीं।
verses.science: अतः उन्होंने जलती आगमें प्रवेश करनेका विचार दर्शये द्विजसूनुं ते मावज्ञात्मानमात्मना॥ २६ किया। जो विषय बार-बार मन में आता है, वही अगली क्रिया की दिशा बनता है। यह पंक्ति उसी मानसिक चयन को अपना विषय बनाती है।

verses.sanskrit: मही नवतृणच्छन्ना शक्रगोपविभूषिता । यौवनस्थेव वनिता स्वं दधारार्तवं वपुः ॥ ६५ ॥
verses.transliteration: mahī navatṛṇacchannā śakragopavibhūṣitā | yauvanastheva vanitā svaṃ dadhārārtavaṃ vapuḥ || 65 ||
verses.hindi: ऐसा करनेसे रोका और कहा--'मैं उन ब्राह्मण-बालकोंको तुम्हें दिखा दूँगा, तुम स्वयं ही अपनी अवज्ञा न करो। ये संसारके मनुष्य तुम्हारी सुविस्तृत कीर्तिकी स्थापना करेंगे'। (अर्जुन कहते हैं--) इस प्रकार स््रेहपूर्वक बात करके माधवने मुझे आश्वासन दिया और उन ब्राह्मणको सान्त्वना देकर सारथिसे यह बात कही-- नामक घोड़ोंको रथमें जोतो।' इस प्रकार उस समय उन्होंने दारुकसे कहा। तदनन्तर रथ जुत जानेपर शूरनन्दन श्रीकृष्णने ब्राह्मणफो रथपर चढ़ा लिया और दारुकको उतारकर मुझसे कहा--'तुम सारथिका काम करो। कौरवश्रेष्ठ ! तत्पश्चात् श्रीकृष्ण, मैं और वह ब्राह्मण तीनों उस रथपर बैठकर सोमपालित उत्तर दिशाकी ओर चल
verses.translation: ²⁸⁸ Literally his prowess and energy.
verses.explanation: ऐसा करनेसे रोका और कहा--'मैं उन ब्राह्मण-बालकोंको तुम्हें दिखा दूँगा, तुम स्वयं ही अपनी अवज्ञा न करो। इस पंक्ति का बल इसी प्रसंग के नियम पर है, किसी अलग प्रसंग से लाई हुई सामान्य उक्ति पर नहीं।
verses.science: ऐसा करनेसे रोका और कहा--'मैं उन ब्राह्मण-बालकोंको तुम्हें दिखा दूँगा, तुम स्वयं ही अपनी अवज्ञा न करो। धीमी श्वास वेगस तंत्रिका को सक्रिय कर भय-प्रतिक्रिया को शांत करती है। यह पंक्ति उसी श्वास और मन के संबंध को कहती है।

verses.sanskrit: अथ सौभपतिः श्रीमान् द्रुमिलो नाम दानवः । भविष्यद्दैवयोगेन विधात्रा तत्र नीयते ॥ ६६ ॥
verses.transliteration: atha saubhapatiḥ śrīmān drumilo nāma dānavaḥ | bhaviṣyaddaivayogena vidhātrā tatra nīyate || 66 ||

verses.sanskrit: कामगेन रथेनाशु तरुणादित्यवर्चसा । यदृच्छया गतस्तत्र सुयामुनदिदृक्षया ॥ ६७ ॥
verses.transliteration: kāmagena rathenāśu taruṇādityavarcasā | yadṛcchayā gatastatra suyāmunadidṛkṣayā || 67 ||

verses.sanskrit: विहायसा कामगमो मनसोऽप्याशुगामिना । स तं प्राप्य पर्वतेन्द्रमवतीर्य रथोत्तमात् ॥ ६८ ॥
verses.transliteration: vihāyasā kāmagamo manaso'pyāśugāminā | sa taṃ prāpya parvatendramavatīrya rathottamāt || 68 ||

verses.sanskrit: पर्वतोपवने न्यस्य रथं पररथारुजम् । अथासौ सूतसहितश्चचार नगमूर्धनि ॥ ६९ ॥
verses.transliteration: parvatopavane nyasya rathaṃ pararathārujam | athāsau sūtasahitaścacāra nagamūrdhani || 69 ||

verses.sanskrit: ततो बहून्यपश्येतां काननानि वनानि च । सर्वर्तुगुणसम्पन्नं नन्दनस्येव काननम् ॥ ७० ॥
verses.transliteration: tato bahūnyapaśyetāṃ kānanāni vanāni ca | sarvartuguṇasampannaṃ nandanasyeva kānanam || 70 ||

verses.sanskrit: चेरतुर्नगशृङ्गेषु कन्दरेषु नदीषु च । नानाधातुपिनद्धैश्च शृङ्गैर्बहुभिरुच्छ्रितैः ॥ ७१ ॥
verses.transliteration: ceraturnagaśṛṅgeṣu kandareṣu nadīṣu ca | nānādhātupinaddhaiśca śṛṅgairbahubhirucchritaiḥ || 71 ||

verses.sanskrit: नानारत्नविचित्रैश्च काञ्चनाञ्जनराजतान् । नानाकुसुमगन्धाढ्यान् नानासत्त्वगणैर्युतान् ॥ ७२ ॥
verses.transliteration: nānāratnavicitraiśca kāñcanāñjanarājatān | nānākusumagandhāḍhyān nānāsattvagaṇairyutān || 72 ||

verses.sanskrit: नानाद्विजगणैर्घुष्टान् नानापुष्पफलद्रुमान् । नानौषधिसमायुक्तानृषिसिद्धानुसेवितान् ॥ ७३ ॥
verses.transliteration: nānādvijagaṇairghuṣṭān nānāpuṣpaphaladrumān | nānauṣadhisamāyuktānṛṣisiddhānusevitān || 73 ||

verses.sanskrit: विद्याधरान् किम्पुरुषानृक्षवानरराक्षसान् । सिंहान् व्याघ्रान् वराहांश्च महिषाञ्छरभाञ्छशान ॥ ७४ ॥
verses.transliteration: vidyādharān kimpuruṣānṛkṣavānararākṣasān | siṃhān vyāghrān varāhāṃśca mahiṣāñcharabhāñchaśāna || 74 ||

verses.sanskrit: सृमरांश्चमरान्न्यङ्कून् मातङ्गान् यक्षराक्षसान् । एवं बहुविधान् पश्यंश्चरमाणो नगोत्तमम् ॥ ७५ ॥
verses.transliteration: sṛmarāṃścamarānnyaṅkūn mātaṅgān yakṣarākṣasān | evaṃ bahuvidhān paśyaṃścaramāṇo nagottamam || 75 ||

verses.sanskrit: दूराद् ददर्श नृपतिर्देवीं देवसुतोपमाम् । क्रीडमानां सखीभिश्च पुष्पं चैव विचिन्वतीम् ॥ ७६ ॥
verses.transliteration: dūrād dadarśa nṛpatirdevīṃ devasutopamām | krīḍamānāṃ sakhībhiśca puṣpaṃ caiva vicinvatīm || 76 ||

verses.sanskrit: ततश्चरन्तीं सुश्रोणीं सस्त्रीभिः सह संवृताम् । दृप्त सौभपतिर्दूराद् विस्मयन् सूतमब्रवीत् ॥ ७७ ॥
verses.transliteration: tataścarantīṃ suśroṇīṃ sastrībhiḥ saha saṃvṛtām | dṛpta saubhapatirdūrād vismayan sūtamabravīt || 77 ||

verses.sanskrit: कस्येयं मृगशावाक्षी वनान्तरविचारिणी । रूपौदार्यगुणोपेता मन्मथस्य रतिर्यथा ॥ ७८ ॥
verses.transliteration: kasyeyaṃ mṛgaśāvākṣī vanāntaravicāriṇī | rūpaudāryaguṇopetā manmathasya ratiryathā || 78 ||

verses.sanskrit: शचीव पुरुहूतस्य उताहो वा तिलोत्तमा । नारायणोरुं निर्भिद्य सम्भूता वरवर्णिनी । ऐलस्य दयिता देवी योषिद्रत्नं किमुर्वशी ॥ ७९ ॥
verses.transliteration: śacīva puruhūtasya utāho vā tilottamā | nārāyaṇoruṃ nirbhidya sambhūtā varavarṇinī | ailasya dayitā devī yoṣidratnaṃ kimurvaśī || 79 ||

verses.sanskrit: क्षीरार्णवे मथ्यमाने सुरासुरगणैः सह । मन्थानं मन्दरं कृत्वामृतार्थमिति नः श्रुतम् ॥ ८० ॥
verses.transliteration: kṣīrārṇave mathyamāne surāsuragaṇaiḥ saha | manthānaṃ mandaraṃ kṛtvāmṛtārthamiti naḥ śrutam || 80 ||

verses.sanskrit: ततोऽमृतात्समुत्तस्थौ देवी श्रीर्लोकभाविनी । नारायणाङ्कलुलिता किं श्रीरेषा वराङ्गना ॥ ८१ ॥
verses.transliteration: tato'mṛtātsamuttasthau devī śrīrlokabhāvinī | nārāyaṇāṅkalulitā kiṃ śrīreṣā varāṅganā || 81 ||

verses.sanskrit: नीलमेघान्तरगता द्योतयन्त्यचिरप्रभा । तथा योषिद्गणान् मध्ये रूपं प्रद्योतयद् वनम् ॥ ८२ ॥
verses.transliteration: nīlameghāntaragatā dyotayantyaciraprabhā | tathā yoṣidgaṇān madhye rūpaṃ pradyotayad vanam || 82 ||

verses.sanskrit: अतीव सुकुमाराङ्गी सुप्रभेन्दुनिभानना । दृष्ट्वा रूपमनिन्द्याङ्ग्या विभ्रान्तो व्याकुलेन्द्रियः ॥ ८३ ॥
verses.transliteration: atīva sukumārāṅgī suprabhendunibhānanā | dṛṣṭvā rūpamanindyāṅgyā vibhrānto vyākulendriyaḥ || 83 ||

verses.sanskrit: कामस्य वशमापन्नो मनो विह्वलतीव मे । भृशं कृन्तति मेऽङ्गानि सायकैः कुसुमायुधः । भित्त्वा हृदि शरान् पञ्च निर्दयं हन्ति मे मनः ॥ ८४ ॥
verses.transliteration: kāmasya vaśamāpanno mano vihvalatīva me | bhṛśaṃ kṛntati me'ṅgāni sāyakaiḥ kusumāyudhaḥ | bhittvā hṛdi śarān pañca nirdayaṃ hanti me manaḥ || 84 ||

verses.sanskrit: हदयाग्निर्वर्धयति आज्यसिक्त इवानलः । कथमद्य भवेत् कार्यं शमार्थं मन्मथाग्निना ॥ ८५ ॥
verses.transliteration: hadayāgnirvardhayati ājyasikta ivānalaḥ | kathamadya bhavet kāryaṃ śamārthaṃ manmathāgninā || 85 ||

verses.sanskrit: केनोपायेन किं कुर्मो भजेन्मां मत्तगामिनी । एवं बहु चिन्तयानो नोपलभ्य च दानवः ॥ ८६ ॥
verses.transliteration: kenopāyena kiṃ kurmo bhajenmāṃ mattagāminī | evaṃ bahu cintayāno nopalabhya ca dānavaḥ || 86 ||

verses.sanskrit: सूतमाह मुहूर्तं तु तिष्ठस्व त्वमिहानघ । अहं यास्यामि तां द्रष्टुं कस्येयमिति योषितम् ॥ ८७ ॥
verses.transliteration: sūtamāha muhūrtaṃ tu tiṣṭhasva tvamihānagha | ahaṃ yāsyāmi tāṃ draṣṭuṃ kasyeyamiti yoṣitam || 87 ||

verses.sanskrit: प्रतीक्षमाणस्तिष्ठस्व यावदागमनं मम । श्रुत्वा तु वचनं तस्य तथास्त्विति वचोऽब्रवीत् ॥ ८८ ॥
verses.transliteration: pratīkṣamāṇastiṣṭhasva yāvadāgamanaṃ mama | śrutvā tu vacanaṃ tasya tathāstviti vaco'bravīt || 88 ||

verses.sanskrit: एवमुक्त्वा दानवेन्द्रो गमनाय मनो दधे । वार्युपस्पृश्य बलवान् ध्यानमेवान्वचिन्तयत् ॥ ८९ ॥
verses.transliteration: evamuktvā dānavendro gamanāya mano dadhe | vāryupaspṛśya balavān dhyānamevānvacintayat || 89 ||

verses.sanskrit: मुहूर्तं ध्यानमात्रेण दृष्टं ज्ञानबलात् ततः । उग्रसेनस्य पत्नीति ज्ञात्वा हर्षमुपागतः ॥ ९० ॥
verses.transliteration: muhūrtaṃ dhyānamātreṇa dṛṣṭaṃ jñānabalāt tataḥ | ugrasenasya patnīti jñātvā harṣamupāgataḥ || 90 ||

verses.sanskrit: उग्रसेनस्य रूपं वै कृत्वा स्वं परिवर्त्य सः । उपासर्पन्महाबाहुः प्रहसन् दानवेश्वरः ॥ ९१ ॥
verses.transliteration: ugrasenasya rūpaṃ vai kṛtvā svaṃ parivartya saḥ | upāsarpanmahābāhuḥ prahasan dānaveśvaraḥ || 91 ||

verses.sanskrit: स्मयमानश्च शनकैर्जग्राहामितवीर्यवान् । उग्रसेनस्य रूपेण मातरं ते व्यधर्षयत् ॥ ९२ ॥
verses.transliteration: smayamānaśca śanakairjagrāhāmitavīryavān | ugrasenasya rūpeṇa mātaraṃ te vyadharṣayat || 92 ||

verses.sanskrit: सा पतिस्निग्धहृदया तं भावेनोपसर्पती । शङ्किता चाभवत्पश्चात्तस्य गौरवदर्शनात् ॥ ९३ ॥
verses.transliteration: sā patisnigdhahṛdayā taṃ bhāvenopasarpatī | śaṅkitā cābhavatpaścāttasya gauravadarśanāt || 93 ||

verses.sanskrit: सा तमाहोत्थिता भीता न त्वं मम पतिर्धुवम् । कस्य त्वं विकृताचारो येनास्मि मलिनीकृता ॥ ९४ ॥
verses.transliteration: sā tamāhotthitā bhītā na tvaṃ mama patirdhuvam | kasya tvaṃ vikṛtācāro yenāsmi malinīkṛtā || 94 ||

verses.sanskrit: एकभर्तृव्रतमिदं मम सन्दूषितं त्वया । पत्युर्मे रूपमास्थाय नीच नीचेन कर्मणा ॥ ९५ ॥
verses.transliteration: ekabhartṛvratamidaṃ mama sandūṣitaṃ tvayā | patyurme rūpamāsthāya nīca nīcena karmaṇā || 95 ||

verses.sanskrit: किं मां वक्ष्यन्ति रुषिता बान्धवाः कुलपांसनीम् । जुगुप्सिता च वत्स्यामि पतिपक्षैर्निराकृता ॥ ९६ ॥
verses.transliteration: kiṃ māṃ vakṣyanti ruṣitā bāndhavāḥ kulapāṃsanīm | jugupsitā ca vatsyāmi patipakṣairnirākṛtā || 96 ||
verses.hindi: द्वारा यात्रा करेंगे! भगवान् श्रीकृष्ण बोले--सरित्पते ! मैंने पूर्वकालमें तुम्हें बर दिया है कि तुम कभी सूखोगे नहीं। मनुष्य तुम्हिरे भीतर रखे हुए नाना प्रकारके रत्नोंके ढेरोंको न जान सकें, इसके लिये तुम केवल अपने जलको स्तम्भित कर लो। साधो! ऐसा करनेसे मैं रथपर बैठा हुआ तुम्हारे ऊपरसे चला जाऊँगा और कोई मनुष्य तुम्हारे रत्नोंका प्रमाण नहीं जान सकेगा॥ १०-११ ॥ तब समुद्रने “तथास्तु” कहकर उनकी बात स्वीकार कर ली। फिर हम सब लोग स्तम्भित हुए जलके मार्गसे चले। वह मार्ग भूमिपर स्थित प्रकाशमान मणियोंकी प्रभासे उद्भासित हो रहा था॥ १२॥ तत्पश्चात् समुद्रको पार करके हम उत्तर कुरुमें जा पहुँचे। फिर एक ही क्षणमें गन्धमादन पर्वतको भी लाँघ गये ॥ १३ ॥ तदनन्तर
verses.translation: ²⁸⁸ Literally his prowess and energy.
verses.explanation: द्वारा यात्रा करेंगे! भगवान् श्रीकृष्ण बोले--सरित्पते ! मैंने पूर्वकालमें तुम्हें बर दिया है कि तुम कभी सूखोगे नहीं। इस पंक्ति का बल इसी प्रसंग के नियम पर है, किसी अलग प्रसंग से लाई हुई सामान्य उक्ति पर नहीं।
verses.science: द्वारा यात्रा करेंगे! भगवान् श्रीकृष्ण बोले--सरित्पते ! मैंने पूर्वकालमें तुम्हें बर दिया है कि तुम कभी सूखोगे नहीं। जो विषय बार-बार मन में आता है, वही अगली क्रिया की दिशा बनता है। यह पंक्ति उसी मानसिक चयन को अपना विषय बनाती है।

verses.sanskrit: धिक्त्वामीदृशमक्षान्तं दुष्कुलं व्युत्थितेन्द्रियम् । अविश्वास्यमनार्यं च परदाराभिमर्शनम् ॥ ९७ ॥
verses.transliteration: dhiktvāmīdṛśamakṣāntaṃ duṣkulaṃ vyutthitendriyam | aviśvāsyamanāryaṃ ca paradārābhimarśanam || 97 ||

verses.sanskrit: स तामाह प्रसज्जन्तीं क्षिप्तः क्रोधेन दानवः । अहं वै द्रुमिलो नाम सौभस्य पतिरूर्जितः ॥ ९८ ॥
verses.transliteration: sa tāmāha prasajjantīṃ kṣiptaḥ krodhena dānavaḥ | ahaṃ vai drumilo nāma saubhasya patirūrjitaḥ || 98 ||

verses.sanskrit: किं मां क्षिपसि रोषेण मूढे पण्डितमानिनि । मानुषं पतिमाश्रित्य नीचं मृत्युवशे स्थितम् ॥ ९९ ॥
verses.transliteration: kiṃ māṃ kṣipasi roṣeṇa mūḍhe paṇḍitamānini | mānuṣaṃ patimāśritya nīcaṃ mṛtyuvaśe sthitam || 99 ||

verses.sanskrit: व्यभिचारान्न दुष्यन्ति स्त्रियः स्त्रीमानगर्विते । न ह्यासां नियता बुद्धिर्मानुषीणां विशेषतः ॥ १०० ॥
verses.transliteration: vyabhicārānna duṣyanti striyaḥ strīmānagarvite | na hyāsāṃ niyatā buddhirmānuṣīṇāṃ viśeṣataḥ || 100 ||

verses.sanskrit: श्रूयन्ते हि स्त्रियो बह्व्यो व्यभिचारव्यतिक्रमैः । प्रसूता देवसङ्काशान् पुत्रान् निश्चलविक्रमान् ॥ १०१ ॥
verses.transliteration: śrūyante hi striyo bahvyo vyabhicāravyatikramaiḥ | prasūtā devasaṅkāśān putrān niścalavikramān || 101 ||

verses.sanskrit: अतीव हि त्वं स्त्रीलोके पतिधर्मवती सती । शुद्धा केशान्विधुन्वन्ती भाषसे यद्यदिच्छसि ॥ १०२ ॥
verses.transliteration: atīva hi tvaṃ strīloke patidharmavatī satī | śuddhā keśānvidhunvantī bhāṣase yadyadicchasi || 102 ||

verses.sanskrit: कस्य त्वमिति यच्चाहं त्वयोक्तो मत्तकाशिनि । कंसस्तस्माद् रिपुध्वंसी तव पुत्रो भविष्यति ॥ १०३ ॥
verses.transliteration: kasya tvamiti yaccāhaṃ tvayokto mattakāśini | kaṃsastasmād ripudhvaṃsī tava putro bhaviṣyati || 103 ||

verses.sanskrit: सा सरोषा पुनर्भूत्वा निन्दन्ती तस्य तं वरम् । उवाच व्यथिता देवी दानवं धृष्टवादिनम् ॥ १०४ ॥
verses.transliteration: sā saroṣā punarbhūtvā nindantī tasya taṃ varam | uvāca vyathitā devī dānavaṃ dhṛṣṭavādinam || 104 ||

verses.sanskrit: धिक ते वृत्तं सुदुर्वृत्त यः सर्वा निन्दसि स्त्रियः । सन्ति स्त्रियो नीचवृत्ताः सन्ति चैव पतिव्रताः ॥ १०५ ॥
verses.transliteration: dhika te vṛttaṃ sudurvṛtta yaḥ sarvā nindasi striyaḥ | santi striyo nīcavṛttāḥ santi caiva pativratāḥ || 105 ||
verses.hindi: दिया ? तथा पर्वतोंमें छेद या अवकाश किस तरह बना दिया 2॥४॥ उस घोर एवं घने अन्धकारको किस प्रकार चक्रसे विदीर्ण किया और वह जो परम उत्कृष्ट तेज था, उसमें आप किस प्रकार प्रविष्ट हुए ? बालकोंका अपहरण किस लिये किया था? और वह कर दिया 2॥ ६॥ केशव ! इतने थोड़े समयमें हमलोगोंका वहाँतक जाना-आना कैसे सम्भव हुआ? यह सब वृत्तान्त मुझे यथार्थरूपसे बताइये' भगवान् श्रीकृष्णने कहा--अर्जुन ! उन महात्मा तेजस्वी पुरुषने मुझे देखनेके लिये ही उन बालकोंका अपहरण किया था। वे जानते थे कि ब्राह्मणोंके कार्यके लिये ही श्रीकृष्ण आयेंगे, अन्यथा नहीं ॥ ८॥ भरतश्रेष्ठ !
verses.translation: ²⁸⁸ Literally his prowess and energy.
verses.explanation: दिया ? तथा पर्वतोंमें छेद या अवकाश किस तरह बना दिया 2॥४॥ उस घोर एवं घने अन्धकारको किस प्रकार चक्रसे विदीर्ण किया और वह जो परम उत्कृष्ट तेज था, उसमें आप किस प…। इस पंक्ति का बल इसी प्रसंग के नियम पर है, किसी अलग प्रसंग से लाई हुई सामान्य उक्ति पर नहीं।
verses.science: दिया ? तथा पर्वतोंमें छेद या अवकाश किस तरह बना दिया 2॥४॥ उस घोर एवं घने अन्धकारको किस प्रकार चक्रसे विदीर्ण किया और वह जो परम उत्कृष्ट तेज था, उसमें आप किस प…। इसे किसी एक घटना का संयोग न मानकर एक नियम की तरह पढ़ना इस पंक्ति का बल है।

verses.sanskrit: यास्त्वेकपत्न्यः श्रूयन्तेऽरुन्धतीप्रमुखाः स्त्रियः । धृता याभिः प्रजाः सर्वा लोकाश्चैव कुलाधम ॥ १०६ ॥
verses.transliteration: yāstvekapatnyaḥ śrūyante'rundhatīpramukhāḥ striyaḥ | dhṛtā yābhiḥ prajāḥ sarvā lokāścaiva kulādhama || 106 ||

verses.sanskrit: यस्त्वया मम पुत्रो वै दत्तो वृत्तविनाशनः । न मे बहुमतस्त्वेष शृणु चापि यदुच्यते ॥ १०७ ॥
verses.transliteration: yastvayā mama putro vai datto vṛttavināśanaḥ | na me bahumatastveṣa śṛṇu cāpi yaducyate || 107 ||

verses.sanskrit: उत्पत्स्यति पुमान् नीच पतिवंशे ममाद्य यः । भविष्यति स ते मृत्युर्यश्च दत्तस्त्वया सुतः ॥ १०८ ॥
verses.transliteration: utpatsyati pumān nīca pativaṃśe mamādya yaḥ | bhaviṣyati sa te mṛtyuryaśca dattastvayā sutaḥ || 108 ||
verses.hindi: रूपमें जो अन्धकार दृष्टिगोचर हुआ था, वह भी मैं ही हूँ॥१३॥ मैं ही घनीभूत अन्धकार और मैं ही उसे विदीर्ण करनेवाला हूँ। मैं ही समस्त भूतोंका काल और मैं ही उनका सनातन धर्म हूँ॥१४॥ चन्द्रमा, हूँ। ये जो चारों दिशाएँ हैं, वे सब-की-सब मेरा ही चतुर्विध रूप हैं॥१५॥ भारत! चारों वर्ण तथा चारों आश्रम मुझसे ही प्रकट हुए हैं। जरायुज, अण्डज, स्वेदद और उद्धिज--इन चार प्रकारके प्राणियोंकी सृष्टि करनेवाला मैं ही हूँ; इस बातको तुम अच्छी तरह जान लो तब मैं ( अर्जुन )-ने कहा-- भगवन्! सर्वभूतेश्वर प्रभो! पुरुषोत्तम! आपको नमस्कार है। मैं आपके स्वरूपोंको भलीभाँति जानना चाहता हूँ; इसीलिये उसके विषयमें आपसे जिज्ञासा करता हूँ और आपकी भगवान् श्रीकृष्णने कहा--पाण्डुनन्दन भारत! ब्रह्म, ब्राह्मण, तप, सत्य, उग्र (संसारबन्धन) और बृहत्तम (कैवल्य)-ये सब मुझसे ही प्रकट होते हैं,
verses.translation: ²⁸⁸ Literally his prowess and energy.
verses.explanation: रूपमें जो अन्धकार दृष्टिगोचर हुआ था, वह भी मैं ही हूँ॥१३॥ मैं ही घनीभूत अन्धकार और मैं ही उसे विदीर्ण करनेवाला हूँ। इस पंक्ति का बल इसी प्रसंग के नियम पर है, किसी अलग प्रसंग से लाई हुई सामान्य उक्ति पर नहीं।
verses.science: रूपमें जो अन्धकार दृष्टिगोचर हुआ था, वह भी मैं ही हूँ॥१३॥ मैं ही घनीभूत अन्धकार और मैं ही उसे विदीर्ण करनेवाला हूँ। धीमी श्वास वेगस तंत्रिका को सक्रिय कर भय-प्रतिक्रिया को शांत करती है। यह पंक्ति उसी श्वास और मन के संबंध को कहती है।

verses.sanskrit: द्रुमिलस्त्वेवमुक्तस्तु जगामाकाशमेव तु । तेनैव रथमुख्येन दिव्येनाप्रतिगामिना ॥ १०९ ॥
verses.transliteration: drumilastvevamuktastu jagāmākāśameva tu | tenaiva rathamukhyena divyenāpratigāminā || 109 ||

verses.sanskrit: जगाम च पुरीं दीना माता तदहरेव ते । मामेवमुक्त्वा भगवान् नारदो मुनिसत्तमः ॥ ११० ॥
verses.transliteration: jagāma ca purīṃ dīnā mātā tadahareva te | māmevamuktvā bhagavān nārado munisattamaḥ || 110 ||

verses.sanskrit: दीप्यमानस्तपोवीर्यात् साक्षादग्निरिव ज्वलन् । वल्लकीं वाद्यमानो हि सप्तस्वरविमूर्च्छिताम् ॥ १११ ॥
verses.transliteration: dīpyamānastapovīryāt sākṣādagniriva jvalan | vallakīṃ vādyamāno hi saptasvaravimūrcchitām || 111 ||

verses.sanskrit: गायनो लक्ष्यवीथीं स जगाम ब्रह्मणोऽन्तिकम् । शृणुष्वेदं महामात्र निबोध वचनं मम ॥ ११२ ॥
verses.transliteration: gāyano lakṣyavīthīṃ sa jagāma brahmaṇo'ntikam | śṛṇuṣvedaṃ mahāmātra nibodha vacanaṃ mama || 112 ||

verses.sanskrit: तथ्यं चोक्तं नारदेन त्रैलोक्यज्ञेन धीमता । अलं बलेन वीर्येण नयेन विनयेन च ॥ ११३ ॥
verses.transliteration: tathyaṃ coktaṃ nāradena trailokyajñena dhīmatā | alaṃ balena vīryeṇa nayena vinayena ca || 113 ||

verses.sanskrit: प्रमाणैर्वापि वीर्येण तेजसा विक्रमेण च । सत्येन चैव दानेन नान्योऽस्ति सदृशः पुमान् ॥ ११४ ॥
verses.transliteration: pramāṇairvāpi vīryeṇa tejasā vikrameṇa ca | satyena caiva dānena nānyo'sti sadṛśaḥ pumān || 114 ||

verses.sanskrit: विदित्वा सर्वमात्मानं वचनं श्रद्दधाम्यहम् । क्ष्रेत्रजोऽहं सुतस्तस्य उग्रसेनस्य हस्तिप ॥ ११५ ॥
verses.transliteration: viditvā sarvamātmānaṃ vacanaṃ śraddadhāmyaham | kṣretrajo'haṃ sutastasya ugrasenasya hastipa || 115 ||

verses.sanskrit: मातापितृभ्यां सन्त्यक्तः स्थापितः स्वेन तेजसा । उभाभ्यामपि विद्विष्टो बान्धवैश्च विशेषतः ॥ ११६ ॥
verses.transliteration: mātāpitṛbhyāṃ santyaktaḥ sthāpitaḥ svena tejasā | ubhābhyāmapi vidviṣṭo bāndhavaiśca viśeṣataḥ || 116 ||

verses.sanskrit: एतानपि हनिष्यामि यादवान् कृष्णपक्षिणः । तदिमौ घातयित्वा तु हस्तिना गोपकिल्बिषौ ॥ ११७ ॥
verses.transliteration: etānapi haniṣyāmi yādavān kṛṣṇapakṣiṇaḥ | tadimau ghātayitvā tu hastinā gopakilbiṣau || 117 ||

verses.sanskrit: तद् गच्छ गजमारुह्य साङ्कुशप्रासतोमरः । स्थिरो भव महामात्र समाजद्वारि मा चिरम् ॥ ११८ ॥
verses.transliteration: tad gaccha gajamāruhya sāṅkuśaprāsatomaraḥ | sthiro bhava mahāmātra samājadvāri mā ciram || 118 ||
verses.hindi: अपने समस्त भाइयोंके साथ राजा युधिष्ठटिरको बड़ा राजभिश्च समासीनैर्ये तत्रासन् समागता:॥ २७  आश्चर्य हुआ था इति श्रीमहाभारते खिलभागे हरिवंशे विष्णुपर्वणि वासुदेवमाहात्म्ये कृष्णार्जुनभाषणे चतुर्दशाधिकशततमोउध्याय: इस प्रकार श्रीमहाभारतके खिलभाग हरिवंशके अन्तर्गत विष्णुपर्वमें वासुदेव-माहात्म्यके प्रसड्भमें श्रीकृष्ण और अर्जुनका संवादविषयक एक सौ चौदहवाँ अध्याय पूरा हुआ भगवान् श्रीकृष्णके पराक्रमोंका संक्षेपसे वर्णन
verses.translation: ²⁸⁸ Literally his prowess and energy.
verses.explanation: अपने समस्त भाइयोंके साथ राजा युधिष्ठटिरको बड़ा राजभिश्च समासीनैर्ये तत्रासन् समागता:॥ २७ आश्चर्य हुआ था इति श्रीमहाभारते खिलभागे हरिवंशे विष्णुपर्वणि वासुदेव…। इस पंक्ति का बल इसी प्रसंग के नियम पर है, किसी अलग प्रसंग से लाई हुई सामान्य उक्ति पर नहीं।
verses.science: अपने समस्त भाइयोंके साथ राजा युधिष्ठटिरको बड़ा राजभिश्च समासीनैर्ये तत्रासन् समागता:॥ २७ आश्चर्य हुआ था इति श्रीमहाभारते खिलभागे हरिवंशे विष्णुपर्वणि वासुदेव…। श्रद्धा और सुरक्षित लगाव तनाव-प्रतिक्रिया को घटाते हैं। यह पंक्ति उसी आश्रय को अपना विषय बनाती है।

verses.sanskrit: नागरिकेभिः पूरितायां रङ्गशालायां मञ्चानां प्रेक्षागृहाणां शोभा, कंसस्य मल्लानां चागमनम्, श्रीकृष्णस्य बलरामस्य च रङ्गद्वारोपरि पदार्पणम्, कुवलयापीड, महामात्र एवं हस्तिनः पादरक्षकानां वधम्, बन्धुद्वयानां रङ्गस्थले प्रवेशः । तस्मिन्नहनि निर्वृत्ते द्वितीये समुपस्थिते । आपूर्यत महारङ्गः पौरैर्युद्धदिदृक्षुभिः ॥ १ ॥
verses.transliteration: nāgarikebhiḥ pūritāyāṃ raṅgaśālāyāṃ mañcānāṃ prekṣāgṛhāṇāṃ śobhā, kaṃsasya mallānāṃ cāgamanam, śrīkṛṣṇasya balarāmasya ca raṅgadvāropari padārpaṇam, kuvalayāpīḍa, mahāmātra evaṃ hastinaḥ pādarakṣakānāṃ vadham, bandhudvayānāṃ raṅgasthale praveśaḥ | tasminnahani nirvṛtte dvitīye samupasthite | āpūryata mahāraṅgaḥ paurairyuddhadidṛkṣubhiḥ || 1 ||

verses.sanskrit: सचित्राष्टास्त्रिचरणाः सार्गलद्वारवेदिकाः । सगवाक्षार्धचन्द्राश्च सुतल्पोत्तमभूषिताः ॥ २ ॥
verses.transliteration: sacitrāṣṭāstricaraṇāḥ sārgaladvāravedikāḥ | sagavākṣārdhacandrāśca sutalpottamabhūṣitāḥ || 2 ||
verses.translation: Vaishampāyana said:—O delighter of the Kurus, on having heard the words of the lord of the celestials, the pious-minded Narada that most eloquent speaker conversant with the essence of virtue, thus spoke:—(1). "O slayer of Vala, O mighty-armed one, I am much concerned in you; and therefore must say what will be conducive to your good (2). As I was aware of your attitude, I told the son of Vasudeva that in days gone by, you had not even given the Parijata tree to the mighty god Siva (3). I tell you truly that I showed him numerous reasons (for not taking down the Parijata tree), but he paid no heed whatever to them (4). 'I am the younger brother of Indra and therefore I claim indulgence at his hands'—these words did that lotus-eyed one tell me in reply. (5) Repeatedly did I, O god, show him numerous reasons; but O slayer of Vritra, still his mind did not change (6). Moreover, O god, the slayer of Madhu that foremost of men, did as if in anger say at the conclusion of his address (7), 'Neither the gods, nor the Gandharvas, nor the Rakshas, nor the Asuras, nor the foremost of the Pannagas, will succeed in attempting to thwart me out of my pledge; O sage mayst thou be attended with all blessings (8)! If Purandara thus requested by thee in a conciliatory manner does not give the Parijata tree to me, then will I hurl my mace at the breast of Purandera on which Sachi besmears fragrant ointments (9).' O Mahendra, this is the firm determination your brother Upendra; now do you do what seems proper and just to you with regard to this matter (10). Hear from me, O lord of the celestials, words that will be conducive to your welfare, as I speak them; it seems to me better to allow the Parijata to be transplanted to Dwarka (11)." O ruler of men, thus spoken to by Narada, the destroyer of all, the thousand-eyed deity, inflamed with wrath, thus addressed him in a clear and distinct voice (12). "O thou of ascetic wealth, if Kesava is bent to behave thus towards me his innocent elder brother, then what harm indeed can he do unto me (13)! O Narada, in times past Krishna committed many acts offensive and insulting to me; I did put up with them all only remembering that he is my brother (14). On the occasion of the burning of the Khandava forest when he drove Arjuna's chariot, he prevented my clouds from extinguishing the raging conflagration (15). He committed an act unpleasant and inimical to my interests by lifting up the Govardhana mountain. When again at the time of slaying Vritra I sought his assistance (16), he replied to me saying—'I am impartial and look equally upon all creatures.' Then I slew Vritra with the help of the strength of my own arms (17). Thou also knowest well, O sage, that when ever war breaks out between the gods and the Asuras Krishna always fights as it pleases his sweet will (ignoring my authority altogether) (18). What is the use of speaking much on the subject? Do thou endeavour to maintain an amicable feeling between ourselves. O Narada, thou art my witness; a rupture among our relatives is remote from my thoughts (19). Keshava might well have been prepared to hurl his mace at my breast (there is nothing untoward in it); but no propriety could be conceived as to why the name of Puloma's daughter was uttered in that connection (20). Our father, the almighty Kasyapa, together with our mother Adity has gone for a sojourn into the waters. This matter ought to be laid before them (21), namely, that my brother Krishna of uncontrolled Self, filled with ignorance and arrogance, has, through the instigation of his wife, abused me his elder brother (who ought to command his regard and obedience) (22). O twice-born one, fie on women, and fie on the influence of arrogance, in as much as, O Vipra, even Vishnu, instigated by his wife, has this day insulted me (23). O mighty sage, it is really surprising that Krishna, overcome by passion and lust, did not pay the slightest regard to the race of our father Kasyapa or to the race of the Sukshnas whence our mother Aditi has sprung, or to the fact of my being his elder brother or to my celestial sovereignty and the respect in which I am held by the gods (24–25). O sinless one, Brahma told me in days past, that a well-behaved and wise brother is to me esteemed more than thousands of sons and wives (26). My father, one of the creators, and my mother Aditi also told me that there is no friend like the brothers, other people are only useless seekers of livelihood (27).²⁹⁰ My father Kasyapa also said, that like the uterine brothers there is no friend in the worlds. The Danavas of sinful propensities fight with me because they are not my brothers (28). What I am now going to tell, O Vipra, ought not be related by me for it contains my own praise; but I may be excused it; I relate it to-day only because there has been an occasion for it (29). O sinless one, in the days of yore, when through the virtue of the boon bestowed on them, the bow-string of Vishnu was not cut off by certain bow-men, and whence thereafter, O foremost of mighty sages, his head was severed off his trunk, it was I who entered into and sustained his body; and when again, with the energy of the Rudras, I succeeded in carefully replacing his head on his trunk, it was Achyuta himself who said that I am the best and foremost among the gods; and then, O Narada, once more remounting his bow with a new string Keshava stood proudly (to face his antagonists) (30–32). O sage, what will my father and my mother tell me if I were to neglect Krishna then,—thinking of his only ancient affection did I, O mighty ascetic, incarnate myself in the body of Krishna (33). O sage, I gave him the Indra's share of the offering of a sacrifice and caused it to be Vaishnava, out of my affection for I look upon him, O Narada, as my younger brother (34). If however unfortunately a battle takes place between me and him, it shall be he, O thou of ascetic wealth that shall strike the first blow—although in other battles, I myself deal it out in as much as I am a sovereign (35). O thou conversant with the essence of religions, I have protected the persons of the regardful Keshava as my own during all his incarnations, O sinless one (36). Dismantling this my residence Vishnu has, with these materials, constructed, O sage, his own _Bhubana_ or world that is superior to all _lokas_ (37). I did not turn my face on that, O sage, out of regard for my brother, and as I always used to think that 'Krishna is a boy and deserves indulgence at my hands' (38). My father and my mother, O Narada, cherish Govinda very much saying—'This my son is a mere child and is youngest in age (39)'. Moreover Keshava is the special favourite of my mother, and, as such, I am very jealous of him. There is not the slightest doubt that the depth of (my mother's) affection reaches its height in Keshava (40). I believed Keshava to be all-knowing, powerful, heroic, and respector of deserving persons; but that belief has proved to be a false one (41). Go thou, O Narada, and tell Keshava these my words; 'Challenged by my enemies I never turn back from a fight (42). Come, if thou wishest, I shall suffer what ever thou mayst desire; O henpecked one, strike the first blow if thou likest it (43). O Janarddana, riding on Garuda and with a firm hand, do thou deal the first blow with thy _Srānga_ mace, or discus or sword (44), O fie, thus struck, O Keshava, I shall strike thee with all my might; if, indeed, my affection does not overwhelm me in the act (45).' Until I am conquered in a battle by the wielder of the discus Krishna, I will not, O foremost of sages, part with the Pārijata tree (46). O thou of ascetic wealth, when he, being younger than I am, challenges me his elder brother to fight, for what reason should I then excuse that henpecked Hari (47)? Do thou, O illustrious sage, go to Dwarkā protected by Krishna, even to-day and tell Achyuta that I am prepared for the quarrel (struggle) (48). O thou, of ascetic wealth, bearing in mind all my words thou shalt thus speak to the slayer of Madhu;—'Until I am conquered by thee I shall not even let thee have a single leaf or its half of the Parijata tree.' O illustrious sage, for my pleasure thou shalt also tell Achyuta fearlessly:—'It behoveth thee not to steal the tree deceitfully; let there be a fair fight; and fie be on crooked practices'" (50).
verses.hindi: बहून्याश्चर्यभूतानि केशवस्य महात्मन:। कथितानि महाबाहो नान्तं शक्यं हि कर्मणाम् विष्णोरमितवीर्यस्य॒ प्रधितोदारकर्मण:। आनृपूर्व्याव्प्रवक्ष्यामि श्रुणुष्वैकमना नूप समुद्रमध्ये दुष्टात्मा नरको दानवो हतः। वासवंचरणे जित्वा पारिजातो हतो बलात् वरुणश्वैव भगवान् निर्जितो लोहितो हदे। दन्तवक्त्रश्न कारूषो निहतो दक्षिणापथे गत्वा च शोणितपुरं शंकरेणाभिरक्षितः

"O slayer of Vala, O mighty-armed one, I am much concerned in you;…
verses.science: बहून्याश्चर्यभूतानि केशवस्य महात्मन:। जो विषय बार-बार मन में आता है, वही अगली क्रिया की दिशा बनता है। यह पंक्ति उसी मानसिक चयन को अपना विषय बनाती है।

verses.sanskrit: प्राङ्मुखैश्चारुनिर्मुक्तैर्माल्यदामावतंसितैः । अलङ्कृतैर्विराजद्भिः शारदैरिव तोयदैः ॥ ३ ॥
verses.transliteration: prāṅmukhaiścārunirmuktairmālyadāmāvataṃsitaiḥ | alaṅkṛtairvirājadbhiḥ śāradairiva toyadaiḥ || 3 ||

verses.sanskrit: मञ्चागारैः सुनिर्युक्तैर्युद्धाय सुविभूषितैः । समाजवाटः शुशुभे समेघौघ इवार्णवः ॥ ४ ॥
verses.transliteration: mañcāgāraiḥ suniryuktairyuddhāya suvibhūṣitaiḥ | samājavāṭaḥ śuśubhe sameghaugha ivārṇavaḥ || 4 ||

verses.sanskrit: स्वकर्मद्रव्ययुक्ताभिः पताकाभिर्निरन्तरम् । श्रेणीनां च गणानां च मञ्चा भान्त्यचलोपमाः ॥ ५ ॥
verses.transliteration: svakarmadravyayuktābhiḥ patākābhirnirantaram | śreṇīnāṃ ca gaṇānāṃ ca mañcā bhāntyacalopamāḥ || 5 ||
verses.translation: O Slayer of Vala, there is no doubt, O god, that disunion among friendly or affectionate brothers causes delight into the hearts of the enemy (9). O foremost of the celestials, those actions only that are connected with a succession of good, should be undertaken; and others, O best of intelligent beings, should be taken in hand after due deliberation (10). Acts which, if begun, would bring repentance in its train, the learned should not at all begin. This is the policy of the wise and intelligent (11). I do not really descry any very good result of this act (viz.), refusal to give Parijata to Krishna. O lord of the immortals, now listen to the reasons thereof (12). That Hari, who doth pervade the world of causes and the world of consequences, and whom the wise know to be the Supreme Soul beyond the influence of Māyā, the manifestation of whom is this universe, is that unmanifest Self and all other conscious beings, have all drawn their consciousness from that Supreme Being Vishnu (13–14).²⁹² The illustrious goddess Umā is the best and principal part of Prakiti and Vishnu is the source of consciousness to all conscious creation; he pervades the manifest universe, and is identified with all objects of enjoyment (15). Like Umā, Rukshmini and other wives of Krishna are his manifest qualities; and the exchangeable Prakriti, and Vishnu and Rudra are all equally possessed of these qualities (gunas) (16). O foremost of gods, there is not the slightest difference between Rudra and Vishnu; and they are the eternal regulators of all qualified creations (_i.e._ all created things endowed with one of more of the qualities of Satwa, Rajas, Tama), and are also the primary qualities (17). The all-creating, highly powerful Vishnu, known also as Adhokshaja, that protector of the worlds, is the creator of the world and the god Maheswara is the destroyer (18). Brahmā and the rest of the celestials and the Prajapatis also have been all created afterwards, O lord of the immortals, by the high-souled Mahādeva (19). That inconceivable, infinite, ancient Purusha Vishnu, who is beyond the qualities themselves, has thus been described in the Vedas (20). In days gone by, the illustrious Vishnu was worshipped by Aditi with great austerities; and he then, pleased with Aditi, bestowed a boon on her (21). "I desire to have thee as a son." This your mother Aditi spoke to the god Nārāyana and after having offered him prayers she bowed down to him(22). Thereupon she was told by him "There is no person equal to myself in the universe; I shall therefore be born as thy son in my own parts (23). Thus, O lord of the celestials, that creator of all, the highly powerful Nārāyana, was born as your brother and he is called Upendra (24). Thus out of his own will did that lord of the past, present and future, the eternal god Hari, create himself in the race of the Kasyapa, because it is in his nature to incarnate himself in this wise (25). That lord of the universe, its creator and destroyer, Keshava has manifested himself in Mathurā out of a desire for the well-being of the world (26). O bestower of honor, as just a lump of Palala is pervaded by a lubricating substance, so is the universe itself pervaded by that wondrous powerful Vishnu (27). That Supreme Brahma, the soul of all, the Protector of all, he that transcends all the gunas (manifested primary elements) being induced by his own desire, incarnates himself in the world and thus produces changes in his own self (28). For these reasons Keshava is to be worshipped by all the celestials; that lotus-navelled almighty and the creator of the people is attended with great praise because he upholds the world in the shape of Ananta. He is also called Sacrifice (_yajna_) by pious reciters of the Vedas (29-30). That Lord assumed a white semblance in the Satya cycle, a red semblance in the Tretā, a yellow semblance in the Dwāpara, and he has now assumed a dark semblance in this Kali cycle (31). This Hari slew Hiranakshya having assumed a divine semblance and this God, out of desire for doing good to the world, upheld the earth when she was sinking into the depth of the waters having assumed the shape of a boar. He slew Hiranyakasipu, in the semblance of the Man-lion (32–33). Assuming the semblance of the Dwarf, Vishnu conquered the world and that auspicious God also bound Vali with serpentine bonds (34). The generous Vishnu, of immeasurable prowess, also usurped for your sake, prosperity that was the common heritage of both the gods and Asuras (both having exerted for its production) (35). Janārddana slays him, whose virtue has waned and it is the vow of that high souled one to kill him who rests on untruth (36). That refuge of the pious, Govinda, who is ever firm in virtue, slew the principal Dānavas, the enemies of the gods, only for the sake of pleasing you (37). That self-contained Being, born as Rāma, slew Rāvana and other Rakshasas like a lion slaying an elephant (38). For the sake of the well-being of the world that lord of the universe, that best of all best beings, still lives in the human world, known by the name of Upendra (39). I have seen Hari wander among the Daityas, wearing matted locks and black deer-skin and bearing a Danda (rod) in his hand, like a raging fire amidst a heap of (dried) grass (40). I have also seen Govinda rid Dānava-ridden world of its Dānavas, for the sake of the well-being of the world (41). O foremost of the gods, Janārddana must take away your Pārijāta tree to Dwarkā. I do not speak untruth (42). You shall not be able to strike Krishna, filled as you are with fraternal affection; nor shall Krishna be able to deal blows on an elder brother like yourself (43). If, O God, you do not like to pay any heed to the words spoken by me, then consult with your other counsellors who are conversant with the rules of polity and are bent on our welfare" (44).
verses.hindi: जाकर महासमरमें उसे पराजित किया और जीवित छोड़ दिया॥ ८--१२॥ उन महात्माने मेरु गिरिमें अग्निदेवपर विजय पायी तथा युद्धमें सौभ विमानके अधिपति राजा शाल्वको जीता और मार गिराया॥ १३॥ फिर सागरमें क्षोभ पैदा करके पञ्चजनको मारकर पाझ्जन्य शट्डुपर अधिकार कर लिया। हयग्रीवका वध किया और अन्य महाबली नरेशोंको भी कालके गालमें डाल दिया जरासंधकी मृत्यु करवाकर सब राजाओंको उसके बन्धनसे मुक्त किया। एकमात्र रथके द्वारा राजाओंको जीतकर गान्धार-राजकुमारीका अपहरण किया पाण्डव अपने राज्यसे भ्रष्ट हो चुके थे और शोकसे आतुर थे, उस अवस्थामें भगवान् श्रीकृष्णने उन सबकी रक्षा की। इन्द्रके घोर खाण्डवबनको अर्जुनद्वारा दग्ध करा दिया॥ १६॥ जनमेजय  फिर अग्निका दिया हुआ गाण्डीव
verses.wordMeaning: O Slayer of Vala, there is no doubt, O god, that disunion among friendly or affectionate brothers causes delight into the hearts of the enemy (9). O foremost of the celestials, those actions only that are connected with a succession of good, should be undertaken; and others,…

O foremost of the celestials, those actions only that are connected with a succession of good, should be undertaken; and others,…
verses.science: जाकर महासमरमें उसे पराजित किया और जीवित छोड़ दिया॥ ८--१२॥ उन महात्माने मेरु गिरिमें अग्निदेवपर विजय पायी तथा युद्धमें सौभ विमानके अधिपति राजा शाल्वको जीता और…। देह के पदार्थ बदलते रहते हैं, पर जानने का बोध बना रहता है। यह पंक्ति उसी अंतर को कहती है।

verses.sanskrit: अन्तःपुरचराणां च प्रेक्षागाराण्यनेकशः । रेजुः काञ्चनचित्राणि रत्नज्वालाकुलानि च ॥ ६ ॥
verses.transliteration: antaḥpuracarāṇāṃ ca prekṣāgārāṇyanekaśaḥ | rejuḥ kāñcanacitrāṇi ratnajvālākulāni ca || 6 ||

verses.sanskrit: तानि रत्नौघक्लृप्तानि ससानुप्रग्रहाणि च । रेजुर्जवनिकाक्षेपैः सपक्षा इव खे नगाः ॥ ७ ॥
verses.transliteration: tāni ratnaughaklṛptāni sasānupragrahāṇi ca | rejurjavanikākṣepaiḥ sapakṣā iva khe nagāḥ || 7 ||
verses.translation: ²⁹¹ Conversant with the rules of worldly conduct and the essentials of
verses.hindi: भयंकर शापसे मुक्त किया। कालयवनको युद्धमें मारा (मुचुकुन्दद्वारा उसका नाश करा दिया) । दो महापराक्रमी दुर्धर्ष वानर मैन्द और द्विविदको तथा ऋक्षराज जाम्बवान्को भी युद्धमें पराजित किया। सान्दीपनिका पुत्र तथा तुम्हारे पिता परीक्षितू-ये दोनों यमराजके वशमें हो गये थे; परंतु उन श्रीकृष्णके तेजसे जीवित हो गये। जनमेजय ! बड़े-बड़े राजाओंका विनाश करनेवाले बहुत-से घोर संग्राम प्राप्त हुए, परंतु उन युद्धोंमें अद्भुत विजय पाकर भगवान् श्रीकृष्णने जिस प्रकार समस्त नरेशोंकों मार गिराया, उसका वर्णन मैं कर चुका हूँ॥ १८--२३॥ इति श्रीमहाभारते खिलभागे हरिवंशे विष्णुपर्वणि वासुदेवमाहात्म्ये पञ्नदशाधिकशततमो5ध्याय:
verses.commentary: Sense: ²⁹¹ Conversant with the rules of worldly conduct and the essentials of
verses.science: भयंकर शापसे मुक्त किया। श्रद्धा और सुरक्षित लगाव तनाव-प्रतिक्रिया को घटाते हैं। यह पंक्ति उसी आश्रय को अपना विषय बनाती है।

verses.sanskrit: तत्र चामरहारैश्च भूषणानां च सिञ्जितैः । मणीनां च विचित्राणां विचित्राश्चेरुरर्चिषः ॥ ८ ॥
verses.transliteration: tatra cāmarahāraiśca bhūṣaṇānāṃ ca siñjitaiḥ | maṇīnāṃ ca vicitrāṇāṃ vicitrāścerurarciṣaḥ || 8 ||

verses.sanskrit: गणिकानां पृथङ्मञ्चाः शुभैरास्तरणाम्बरैः । शोभिता वारमुख्याभिर्विमानप्रतिमौजसः ॥ ९ ॥
verses.transliteration: gaṇikānāṃ pṛthaṅmañcāḥ śubhairāstaraṇāmbaraiḥ | śobhitā vāramukhyābhirvimānapratimaujasaḥ || 9 ||
verses.translation: Vaishampāyana said:—On coming to the beautiful city of Dwarka, that foremost of all sages, Nārada, saw that foremost of beings, that subduer of his foes, Nārāyana (1) comfortably seated with Satyabhāmā in his own mansion, and appearing highly beautiful in consequence of his charming form that transcended all energies (2). He saw the high-souled Keshava of firm vows engrossed in that thought (_i.e._, of the Pārijāta), and only gratifying the lovely Satyabhāmā with empty words (3). On seeing Nārada, the divine Adhokshaja rose (from his seat) and worshipped him with prescribed ceremonies (4). After Nārada had been comfortably seated, having cast off the fatigue (of the journey) the slayer of Madhu smilingly questioned him on the subject of the Pārijāta tree (5). Thereupon, O Janamejaya, that sage, possessed of ascetic merit, told the younger brother of Indra all his words in full details (6). Having heard all those words from Nārada, Krishna spoke to him thus: "Even to-morrow shall I go to the region of the celestials, O foremost of all virtuous sages" (7). Having spoken this much only Hari entered into the waters of the ocean, accompanied by Nārada; and there in secret he again addressed him thus (8):—"Going to-day to the residence of Mahendra, and offering him my best regards, do thou, O sage, tell that foremost of immortals, the high-souled Indra, these my very words (9). 'O Sakra, O lord I know me determined as regards the fetching down of the Pārijāta here; and if a fight does actually take place, thou shalt not be able to stand before me (even for a moment.)'" (10).
verses.hindi: यो5भिगुप्त: स्वयं ब्रह्मज्छड्ट्रेण महात्मना। सहवासं गतेनैव सगणेन गुहेन तु जनमेजयने कहा--विद्वानोंमें उत्तम द्विजश्रेष्ठ ! मैंने आपके मुखसे बुद्धिमान् महाबाहु यदुकुलसिंह वसुदेवनन्दन श्रीकृष्फेक अपरिमेय कर्मोको फिरसे सुना। तपोधन! आपने पहले महान् असुर बाणके विषयमें जो चर्चा की है, उसको मैं विस्तारसे सुनना चाहता हूँ। ब्रह्मन्! वह असुर देवाधिदेव महादेवजीके पुत्रभावको कैसे प्राप्त हुआ ? जिससे महात्मा भगवान् शट्डूरने स्वयं उसकी रक्षा की तथा उसके सहवासमें रहनेवाले गणोंसहित भगवान् स्कन्दने भी उसका संरक्षण किया॥ १--४॥ बलवान बलिका पुत्र जो अपने सौ भाइयोंमें ज्येष्ट था, वह सैकड़ों दिव्यास्त्र धारण करनेवाली सहस्न भुजाओंसे युक्त था

verses.science: यो5भिगुप्त: स्वयं ब्रह्मज्छड्ट्रेण महात्मना। जो विषय बार-बार मन में आता है, वही अगली क्रिया की दिशा बनता है। यह पंक्ति उसी मानसिक चयन को अपना विषय बनाती है।

verses.sanskrit: तत्रासनानि ख्यातानि पर्यङ्काश्च हिरण्मयाः । प्रकीर्णाश्च कुथाश्चित्राः सपुष्पस्तबकैर्वृताः ॥ १० ॥
verses.transliteration: tatrāsanāni khyātāni paryaṅkāśca hiraṇmayāḥ | prakīrṇāśca kuthāścitrāḥ sapuṣpastabakairvṛtāḥ || 10 ||

verses.sanskrit: सौवर्णाः पानकुम्भाश्च पानभूम्यश्च शोभिताः । फलावदंशपूर्णाश्च चाङ्गेर्यः पानयोजिताः ॥ ११ ॥
verses.transliteration: sauvarṇāḥ pānakumbhāśca pānabhūmyaśca śobhitāḥ | phalāvadaṃśapūrṇāśca cāṅgeryaḥ pānayojitāḥ || 11 ||
verses.translation: Kashyapa said:"—To him whose foot-falls are mighty,²⁹³ who is the nascent cause of the universe, who is the Supreme, who is the creator of the world (potent cause), who is attained only through virtue (Dharma), who is the Lord of grace (_i.e._, metes out grace to them who worship and adore him), who is Self-controlled and endued with divine energy—I bow down to that illustrious lord of the universe (29). He is the lord of the celestials. He is the destroyer of sin. Through his instrumentality the universe extends, He being the cause nascent and potential. The image of His intelligence, the sacred waters hold.²⁹⁴ I seek refuge with the Supreme ruler of the universe (30). He, who under the semblance of a self-controlled ascetic, slew the uncontrolled who were ignorant of the doctrines of the Vedanta and tried to do away with the friendly qualities, He, whose semblance is delightful, and whose origin is sacred, I seek the protection of that lord of the universe with my (bent) head (31). That great and undisputed Master of the universe, who takes under his benign protection the advanced (_i.e._, that is morally and religiously) section of worldly beings, He who is the Light of all lights. He, who is identified with the semblance of Brahma known by the designation of Sukrita—is immutable and indomitable; that bestower of boons on those sages who perform penances living upon the juice of the Soma plant and the beams of the moon; may that Being nourish me with his Eternal Energy! (32) He who is demonstrated in the Atharva Veda; He whose heads²⁹⁵ are beautiful, He who is the origin of the beings, who is accomplished, heroic, and destroyer of the Danavas; He who in sacrifices is the sanctified sacrificial burnt offering;—I do seek the refuge of that Divine Being, the Lord of the universe (33). He in whom this illusory universal net is woven; He who is the universe and its soul; He who discovers happiness for his votaries and travels in a vehicle that soars high in the heavens; may that Lord of the universe be ever graciously pleased with me, (or be the source of constant happiness to me) (34). I do bow down to the furious Mahādeva who wanders in our hearts, who is Absolute Intelligence whose branches (the Vedas that have come out of Him) are all beautiful, who is the highly powerful leader of virtue, worshipful, thousand-eyed, distributer of fruits of actions done in a hundred different ways, and who is the creator of the worlds (35). He that is pure (unconsorted) attainable through Yoga, praised in the Vedas, beyond the reach of sin, the cause of destruction, the source of the world's weal and woe, the Lord of all creation, the upholder of the burden of the universe, the master of the senses, and the resort of the destructive agencies (such as time, &c.,) I do approach, with a bent head, that god whose forehead is beautified with a crescent (36). He who wields the trident, who gives fruition (of acts) soon, who reduces the influence of the evil passions and increases such qualities as quietude, &c., who is identical with such pious acts as sacrifices, &c., who is that quality of religious merit through which sins dwindle away soon, who is the recipient of the fruits of religious merit consequent on deeds performed with sanctity and the principle of goodness, who is the real essence of all, and who has taken the vow (of purity)—I do seek protection from him (37). He who is infinite in energy, who is the upholder of all actions, the Primary Being, who is (unlike other gods) free from sacrificial modes, and is endowed with knowledge—He who is the cause of the commencement of sacrifices by sacrificial priests, the eater of sacrificial _Havis_; who is the first-born in the universe, and the eldest of creation, and who is like a Brāhmana among the pious—I do seek his refuge (38). He who transcends the _Gunas_ (the elements of creation), who is like Vishnu the son of Prisni, who transcends the illusory creation—and agitates the universe through his beatitude, whose semblance is charming; who is of pure self, who is also—but intelligence, who practises _Maya_ in dealing with the wicked—I bow down to him (39). I bow down to Him who is the Omkara of half syllables of the Yogis who is free from harmful acts and the identity of Virtue, who is firm in vow, and in (handing) the bow, who is the act of throwing, who is heroic, accomplished in bowmanship, beyond the reach of weapons and the Lord of the living creation, and its destroyer (40). He who is without a second (sole matchless) the friend of all, the past and the future, the discoverer of _Havi_, (sacrificial burnt offerings), in the shape of fire, the destroyer of all passions as lust, &c., the slayer of Rākshasas, who is undivisible, and the divider,—may that illustrious God protect me (41). That one Lord of the worlds, who though one—enters into every thing of the universe, that one who gave the vital breaths (Maruts) their life, breath, (i.e., he who is the life of life), he who, out of his innate harmlessness, is ever attended upon by friendliness and amiability, may that god of good actions lead me to-day to blessings and happiness (42). He, who in the shape of Brahmā, created the Satyaloka together with the essence of goodness, and the entire illusory universe, who is all-cognizant and the knower of Brahma and is endowed with six excellences, whose semblance is numerous, in his different enemy-destroying incarnations, may that god protect me! (43) He who is the revealer of the supersensuous and the sensuous objects, who is increate and self-sufficient, who is entire and undivided who is in contact with the sense-objects, the granter of prosperities, the giver of life, the wearer of deer-skin, who is Supreme Ecstacy, the life of the blowing winds, the receptacle of conception, the creator of happiness—may that Lord bless me accompanied by his two wives (44). He who posseses three eyes, who gives nourishment, who, to inculcate religion to the twice-born ones, accords boons to the sacrificers, He who is the most excellent of the excellent the winner of victory in battles, the Lord, the God of the gods,—I resort to the protection of that Rudra (45). He that is the mouth of the gods in the shape of fire, the destroyer of the evil doers, who is the _Soma_ sacrifice, the annihilator of the tree of Mundane Existence, the witness of all the actions, the source of dissolution of all things,—I seek refuge with that Lord of Beings, Rudra, the knower of the _Gunas_ and their repository (46). He who is prideless, the performer of sacrifices, the beginning, the middle and the end of the worlds, the condition of peace and unification,—he who is sung in the sacrifices prescribed in the Vedas as numerous different gods, and He who is the regulator even of the celestial world, I seek refuge with that Rudra (47). He who is the wearer of the elephant-skin, the performer of vows and observances, who is decorated with a zone, who is easily pleasable, the controller of anger free from sin, ever-existent, and the Supreme Soul, who is immanent in Nature, the wearer of matted locks, I bow, down to that Lord, the adorable of the adorable (48). The god of gods, the holy of holies, the sacrifice of sacrifices, the greatest of the great, He of hundred (infinite) semblances, the Master of all the masters of the senses, (i.e., eye of eyes, ear of ears, &c.,) the ever-praised one, I seek refuge with him. (49). He who is the wonder of all hearts, the Purusha of mysterious appellation, the self-manifest _Pranava_, who is revealed even in the absence of such revealing agencies as light and the eyes, &c., and He, who is the potent cause of the divine image known as _Jiva_, I bow down to that god endued with the qualities and the repository of all bliss (50). He who is the producer of the both (matter and mind) but is himself unproduced, (or He from whom matter and mind have been born but who did not produce them, He transcending all causes) who is subtle (inconceivable) and simultaneously the same with and different from all created beings (unified and differentiated) who is self-existent, the place of dissolution of existence, the benign Giver who is sweetness, ecstacy and beatitude, may He protect me (51). He who is near to every body, and revealed to those who are possessed of _Sadhana_, who is the bestower of such knowledge as 'I am absolute', to those who reverentially believe in Him, the presiding Deity of the great and the good actions, He who is fulfiller of the desires and the fulfillment of the Six Excellences, may that Lord protect me (52). He who is destroyer of the mental and physical sources of pain, the efficient as well as the material cause, the evolver (of the passions) may that God of gods, that one possessed of Supreme Energy, cut off the cause of pain of me and of the pious, wielding his potent weapons (53). By whom in the days of yore the guileful Danavas who used to give much pain to the gods, were cut with dreadful arrows and eradicated as so many thorns, may that upholder of the water of the universe, that Supreme Lord, protect me! (54)
verses.hindi: यथा चास्य वरो दत्त: शंकरेण महात्मना यथा च देवदेवस्य पुत्रत्व॑ सोडसुरो गतः। यदर्थ च महद् युद्ध तत् सर्वमखिलं श्रुणु तस्य बुद्धिः समुत्पन्ना तपश्चर्तु सुदुष्करम्। रुद्रस्थाराधनार्थाय देवस्य स्यां यथा सुतः देवश्व परमं॑ तोषं जगाम च सहोमया

verses.explanation: यथा चास्य वरो दत्त: शंकरेण महात्मना यथा च देवदेवस्य पुत्रत्व॑ सोडसुरो गतः। इस पंक्ति का बल इसी प्रसंग के नियम पर है, किसी अलग प्रसंग से लाई हुई सामान्य उक्ति पर नहीं।
verses.science: यथा चास्य वरो दत्त: शंकरेण महात्मना यथा च देवदेवस्य पुत्रत्व॑ सोडसुरो गतः। जो विषय बार-बार मन में आता है, वही अगली क्रिया की दिशा बनता है। यह पंक्ति उसी मानसिक चयन को अपना विषय बनाती है।

verses.sanskrit: अन्ये च मञ्चा बहवः काष्ठसञ्चयबन्धनाः । रेजुः प्रस्तरणास्तत्र शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः ॥ १२ ॥
verses.transliteration: anye ca mañcā bahavaḥ kāṣṭhasañcayabandhanāḥ | rejuḥ prastaraṇāstatra śataśo'tha sahasraśaḥ || 12 ||

verses.sanskrit: उत्तमागारिकाश्चैव सूक्ष्मजालावलोकिनः । स्त्रीणां प्रेक्षागृहा भान्ति राजहंसा इवाम्बरे ॥ १३ ॥
verses.transliteration: uttamāgārikāścaiva sūkṣmajālāvalokinaḥ | strīṇāṃ prekṣāgṛhā bhānti rājahaṃsā ivāmbare || 13 ||

verses.sanskrit: प्राङ्मुखश्चारुनिर्मुक्तो मेरुशृङ्गसमप्रभः । रुक्मपत्रनिभस्तम्भश्चित्रनिर्योगशोभितः ॥ १४ ॥
verses.transliteration: prāṅmukhaścārunirmukto meruśṛṅgasamaprabhaḥ | rukmapatranibhastambhaścitraniryogaśobhitaḥ || 14 ||

verses.sanskrit: प्रेक्षागारः स कंसस्य प्रचकाशेऽधिकं श्रिया । शोभितो माल्यदामैश्च निवासकृतलक्षणः ॥ १५ ॥
verses.transliteration: prekṣāgāraḥ sa kaṃsasya pracakāśe'dhikaṃ śriyā | śobhito mālyadāmaiśca nivāsakṛtalakṣaṇaḥ || 15 ||
verses.hindi: राज्यं प्रशासते नित्यं क्षोभयन् सर्वदेवता: अचिन्तयन् देवगणान् युद्धमाकाइ्क्षते सदा नदेवानच गन्धर्वा न यक्षा नापि पन्नगाः । तस्य युद्धे व्यतिष्ठन्त देवदेवस्थ तेजसा ज्यम्बकेणाभिगुप्तश्न दर्पोत्सिक्तो महासुरः। भूयो मृगयते युद्धं शूलिनं सो5भ्यगच्छत।
verses.translation: Kashyapa said:"—To him whose foot-falls are mighty,²⁹³ who is the nascent cause of the universe, who is the Supreme, who is the creator of the world (potent cause), who is attained only through virtue (Dharma), who is the Lord of grace (_i.e._, metes out grace to them who worship and adore him), who is Self-controlled and endued with divine energy—I bow down to that illustrious lord of the universe (29). He is the lord of the celestials. He is the destroyer of sin. Through his instrumentality the universe extends, He being the cause nascent and potential. The image of His intelligence, the sacred waters hold.²⁹⁴ I seek refuge with the Supreme ruler of the universe (30). He, who under the semblance of a self-controlled ascetic, slew the uncontrolled who were ignorant of the doctrines of the Vedanta and tried to do away with the friendly qualities, He, whose semblance is delightful, and whose origin is sacred, I seek the protection of that lord of the universe with my (bent) head (31). That great and undisputed Master of the universe, who takes under his benign protection the advanced (_i.e._, that is morally and religiously) section of worldly beings, He who is the Light of all lights. He, who is identified with the semblance of Brahma known by the designation of Sukrita—is immutable and indomitable; that bestower of boons on those sages who perform penances living upon the juice of the Soma plant and the beams of the moon; may that Being nourish me with his Eternal Energy! (32) He who is demonstrated in the Atharva Veda; He whose heads²⁹⁵ are beautiful, He who is the origin of the beings, who is accomplished, heroic, and destroyer of the Danavas; He who in sacrifices is the sanctified sacrificial burnt offering;—I do seek the refuge of that Divine Being, the Lord of the universe (33). He in whom this illusory universal net is woven; He who is the universe and its soul; He who discovers happiness for his votaries and travels in a vehicle that soars high in the heavens; may that Lord of the universe be ever graciously pleased with me, (or be the source of constant happiness to me) (34). I do bow down to the furious Mahādeva who wanders in our hearts, who is Absolute Intelligence whose branches (the Vedas that have come out of Him) are all beautiful, who is the highly powerful leader of virtue, worshipful, thousand-eyed, distributer of fruits of actions done in a hundred different ways, and who is the creator of the worlds (35). He that is pure (unconsorted) attainable through Yoga, praised in the Vedas, beyond the reach of sin, the cause of destruction, the source of the world's weal and woe, the Lord of all creation, the upholder of the burden of the universe, the master of the senses, and the resort of the destructive agencies (such as time, &c.,) I do approach, with a bent head, that god whose forehead is beautified with a crescent (36). He who wields the trident, who gives fruition (of acts) soon, who reduces the influence of the evil passions and increases such qualities as quietude, &c., who is identical with such pious acts as sacrifices, &c., who is that quality of religious merit through which sins dwindle away soon, who is the recipient of the fruits of religious merit consequent on deeds performed with sanctity and the principle of goodness, who is the real essence of all, and who has taken the vow (of purity)—I do seek protection from him (37). He who is infinite in energy, who is the upholder of all actions, the Primary Being, who is (unlike other gods) free from sacrificial modes, and is endowed with knowledge—He who is the cause of the commencement of sacrifices by sacrificial priests, the eater of sacrificial _Havis_; who is the first-born in the universe, and the eldest of creation, and who is like a Brāhmana among the pious—I do seek his refuge (38). He who transcends the _Gunas_ (the elements of creation), who is like Vishnu the son of Prisni, who transcends the illusory creation—and agitates the universe through his beatitude, whose semblance is charming; who is of pure self, who is also—but intelligence, who practises _Maya_ in dealing with the wicked—I bow down to him (39). I bow down to Him who is the Omkara of half syllables of the Yogis who is free from harmful acts and the identity of Virtue, who is firm in vow, and in (handing) the bow, who is the act of throwing, who is heroic, accomplished in bowmanship, beyond the reach of weapons and the Lord of the living creation, and its destroyer (40). He who is without a second (sole matchless) the friend of all, the past and the future, the discoverer of _Havi_, (sacrificial burnt offerings), in the shape of fire, the destroyer of all passions as lust, &c., the slayer of Rākshasas, who is undivisible, and the divider,—may that illustrious God protect me (41). That one Lord of the worlds, who though one—enters into every thing of the universe, that one who gave the vital breaths (Maruts) their life, breath, (i.e., he who is the life of life), he who, out of his innate harmlessness, is ever attended upon by friendliness and amiability, may that god of good actions lead me to-day to blessings and happiness (42). He, who in the shape of Brahmā, created the Satyaloka together with the essence of goodness, and the entire illusory universe, who is all-cognizant and the knower of Brahma and is endowed with six excellences, whose semblance is numerous, in his different enemy-destroying incarnations, may that god protect me! (43) He who is the revealer of the supersensuous and the sensuous objects, who is increate and self-sufficient, who is entire and undivided who is in contact with the sense-objects, the granter of prosperities, the giver of life, the wearer of deer-skin, who is Supreme Ecstacy, the life of the blowing winds, the receptacle of conception, the creator of happiness—may that Lord bless me accompanied by his two wives (44). He who posseses three eyes, who gives nourishment, who, to inculcate religion to the twice-born ones, accords boons to the sacrificers, He who is the most excellent of the excellent the winner of victory in battles, the Lord, the God of the gods,—I resort to the protection of that Rudra (45). He that is the mouth of the gods in the shape of fire, the destroyer of the evil doers, who is the _Soma_ sacrifice, the annihilator of the tree of Mundane Existence, the witness of all the actions, the source of dissolution of all things,—I seek refuge with that Lord of Beings, Rudra, the knower of the _Gunas_ and their repository (46). He who is prideless, the performer of sacrifices, the beginning, the middle and the end of the worlds, the condition of peace and unification,—he who is sung in the sacrifices prescribed in the Vedas as numerous different gods, and He who is the regulator even of the celestial world, I seek refuge with that Rudra (47). He who is the wearer of the elephant-skin, the performer of vows and observances, who is decorated with a zone, who is easily pleasable, the controller of anger free from sin, ever-existent, and the Supreme Soul, who is immanent in Nature, the wearer of matted locks, I bow, down to that Lord, the adorable of the adorable (48). The god of gods, the holy of holies, the sacrifice of sacrifices, the greatest of the great, He of hundred (infinite) semblances, the Master of all the masters of the senses, (i.e., eye of eyes, ear of ears, &c.,) the ever-praised one, I seek refuge with him. (49). He who is the wonder of all hearts, the Purusha of mysterious appellation, the self-manifest _Pranava_, who is revealed even in the absence of such revealing agencies as light and the eyes, &c., and He, who is the potent cause of the divine image known as _Jiva_, I bow down to that god endued with the qualities and the repository of all bliss (50). He who is the producer of the both (matter and mind) but is himself unproduced, (or He from whom matter and mind have been born but who did not produce them, He transcending all causes) who is subtle (inconceivable) and simultaneously the same with and different from all created beings (unified and differentiated) who is self-existent, the place of dissolution of existence, the benign Giver who is sweetness, ecstacy and beatitude, may He protect me (51). He who is near to every body, and revealed to those who are possessed of _Sadhana_, who is the bestower of such knowledge as 'I am absolute', to those who reverentially believe in Him, the presiding Deity of the great and the good actions, He who is fulfiller of the desires and the fulfillment of the Six Excellences, may that Lord protect me (52). He who is destroyer of the mental and physical sources of pain, the efficient as well as the material cause, the evolver (of the passions) may that God of gods, that one possessed of Supreme Energy, cut off the cause of pain of me and of the pious, wielding his potent weapons (53). By whom in the days of yore the guileful Danavas who used to give much pain to the gods, were cut with dreadful arrows and eradicated as so many thorns, may that upholder of the water of the universe, that Supreme Lord, protect me! (54)

verses.sanskrit: तस्मिन् नानाजनाकीर्णे जनौघप्रतिनादिते । समाजवाटे संस्तब्धे कम्पमानार्णवप्रभे ॥ १६ ॥

verses.sanskrit: राजा कुवलयापीडः समाजद्वारि कुञ्जरः । तिष्ठत्विति समाज्ञाप्य प्रेक्षागारमुपाययौ ॥ १७ ॥
verses.transliteration: rājā kuvalayāpīḍaḥ samājadvāri kuñjaraḥ | tiṣṭhatviti samājñāpya prekṣāgāramupāyayau || 17 ||

verses.sanskrit: स शुक्ले वाससी बिभ्रच्छवेतव्यजनचामरः । शुशुभे श्वेतमुकुटः श्वेताभ्र इव चन्द्रमाः ॥ १८ ॥
verses.transliteration: sa śukle vāsasī bibhracchavetavyajanacāmaraḥ | śuśubhe śvetamukuṭaḥ śvetābhra iva candramāḥ || 18 ||
verses.hindi: वृषभध्वज रुद्रदेवके पास जाकर उन्हें प्रणाम और अभिवादन करनेके पश्चात् बलिपुत्र बाणने उनसे यह बात पूछी-- ॥ २५॥ “प्रभो! आपका सहारा पाकर सेनासहित मैंने बलके मद और अभिमानपूर्वक साध्यों और मरुदू- गणोंसहित देवताओंको अनेक बार परास्त किया है वे मुझे पराजित करनेकी ओरसे तो निराश हैं; परंतु मेरे द्वारा पुनः पराजित होनेके भयसे डरे हुए हैं, अत: इस देशमें आकर इसी नगरमें सुखपूर्वक निवास करते हैं साथ ही मेरी आज्ञा ले स्वर्गमें भी जाकर वहाँ सुखपूर्वक रहते हैं, अतः मैं युद्धसे निराश हो गया हूँ। अब युद्ध न मिलनेसे मुझे जीवित रहनेकी इच्छा नहीं होती ॥ २८ ॥ यदि युद्धका सुयोग न मिला तो मेरे लिये इन सहस्र भुजाओंका बोझ ढोना व्यर्थ है; अत: बताइये, कया मुझे युद्धका अवसर प्राप्त हो सकता है ? देव ! युद्धके बिना मेरा मन कहीं नहीं लग रहा है। अतः इसके लिये मुझपर कृपा कीजिये '
